# What is Going on at the Michigan Secretary of State Office???
---
Friends, Michigan's Secretary of State office is a mess.
It seems to be plagued with disorder, lack of long term planning, and unreliable vendors. It is run by Secretary of State Benson who wants to be your next Governor. But Lt. Governor Gilchrist, who claims to be an expert at software engineer and programming -- and is currently #2 in Michigan's line up of leadership, has not stepped in to help.
Is it because he has not showed up for work? Is it because he has somehow missed some of the obvious issues that impact our citizens? He is at least aware of some things that have gone wrong with the office. Recently he noted on the For The Sake of Argument Podcast with Lori Goldman that the next Secretary of State must fix Jocelyn Benson's $9,000,000 transparency website.
Why has he, as an elected leader not done more to date? There have been many issues over the last 8 years with the Secretary's office.
Let me explain one of the biggest snafus yet:
---

---
When I am elected as your next Secretary of State I will:
* Improve transparency
* Demonstrate reliability - I will show up to work
* Remove politics from the office

I will make sure that you are served well. I have the experience to know what needs to be done and will be effective on Day 1.
Our citizens and our clerks deserve to have fair playing rules regardless of Political Party, and a Secretary of State office that will be a real partner so they can accomplish their tasks.
A vote for me is a vote for you!

Anthony G. Forlini Republican Candidate for Secretary of State

### What AI, China and global instability are revealing about where capital goes next
| | [Patrick J. Murphy](https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa)
---
| Sep 15

For most of the past generation, American business leaders and investors were rewarded for thinking about globalization primarily through the lens of efficiency. Goods moved easily across borders, capital followed opportunity, and supply chains stretched across oceans with remarkably little friction. If a component could be manufactured more cheaply somewhere else, that was usually taken as evidence that the system was doing its job.
For a long time, it did.
But the assumptions underneath that system have become harder to take for granted. Wars have disrupted shipping routes that once seemed dependable. Cyberattacks have demonstrated that infrastructure thousands of miles from a battlefield can become part of the conflict. A shortage of a single component can stop an entire production line. And China's rise has turned semiconductors, energy, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing and artificial intelligence from ordinary commercial considerations into questions of great-power competition.
Consider the Strait of Hormuz. Roughly 20.9 million barrels of oil a day moved through it in the first half of 2025, equivalent to about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption and roughly one-quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade. Yet the available pipelines capable of bypassing the strait could handle only a fraction of that volume. One narrow waterway is a reminder of how much of the global economy still depends on physical infrastructure that investors largely take for granted until something goes wrong.
The political response to these vulnerabilities is already reshaping the economic landscape. The Trump administration has put tariffs, domestic manufacturing and economic security at the center of its trade agenda, while treating dependence in areas such as semiconductors and critical minerals as a strategic vulnerability. President Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping later this month, with technology and artificial intelligence among the major issues hanging over the relationship. At home, data centers themselves are becoming a political issue as Americans head toward the midterm elections.
Taken together, these debates are forcing a question that business leaders and investors could once largely avoid: what does America actually need to be able to build for itself, and what can we safely rely on others to provide?
None of this means globalization is ending. But I do believe cheap globalization is.
By that I mean the era when the lowest price could reasonably be treated as the true cost. A factory thousands of miles away may still offer the cheapest unit price, but the calculation changes when the product has to travel through a vulnerable shipping route, when a critical input is controlled by a strategic competitor, or when production cannot be replaced quickly during a crisis.
Efficiency still matters. It always will. What has changed is that resilience now has an economic value, and markets are beginning to put a price on it.
I'm in Los Angeles this week speaking with private-market investors at SuperReturn US West, and that is the argument I wanted to put in front of them. For much of my adult life, geopolitics would have been a fairly specialized subject at an investment conference. Today, it belongs much closer to the beginning of the investment memo.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d07d253-2fe2-4c63-a4cd-049595a6f0d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The question for investors is no longer simply where capital can find the greatest efficiency. It is where the vulnerabilities of the global economy are beginning to create scarcity, durable demand and, ultimately, opportunity.
## **Economic Capacity Is National Power**
I have seen American economic power from several different vantage points over the years, first as a deployed soldier in Bosnia and Iraq, later in Congress and at the Pentagon, and now in the private sector. Those experiences have convinced me that we have spent too much time treating economic capacity and national power as separate subjects.
There is an old Pentagon saying that amateurs talk strategy and professionals talk logistics. Like most military aphorisms, it has lasted because reality keeps proving it right. The United States can develop the most sophisticated weapons system in the world, but its strategic value changes considerably if we cannot replace its parts, replenish ammunition, move equipment where it needs to go or increase production during a crisis. If one obscure component buried deep in the supply chain comes from a country we may not be able to rely upon during a conflict, that dependency matters whether or not anyone noticed it on a spreadsheet five years earlier.
Our allies have reached much the same conclusion. NATO's new defense investment commitment calls for allies to reach [5% of GDP](https://substack.com/redirect/2c636f7d-cc05-4410-bd8c-89d1e0ceaadd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) annually by 2035, with at least 3.5% devoted to core defense and up to another 1.5% for critical infrastructure, networks, civil preparedness, resilience, innovation and the defense industrial base. European allies and Canada increased combined defense expenditures by nearly 20% in real terms in 2025.
That is a significant amount of capital moving toward capacity, and it reflects a broader realization that national security is no longer principally about buying more weapons. It is also about having the factories, infrastructure, technology, logistics and supply chains necessary to produce and sustain them.
The private sector is discovering versions of the same lesson. We saw it when automakers had vehicles sitting unfinished because they could not get enough semiconductors. We see it when utilities wait for transformers and other critical equipment. A supply chain can be extraordinarily efficient until the moment it stops working.
That is why investors increasingly need to understand logistics, industrial capacity and geopolitical exposure as part of the investment thesis rather than as risks to be considered after it.
## **AI Is Repricing the Physical Economy**
There is an irony at the center of the artificial-intelligence revolution that I think investors should pay particular attention to: the most advanced digital technology the world has ever developed is making the physical economy more valuable.
For years, investors were rewarded for finding businesses that could become increasingly asset-light. Manufacturing could be outsourced, inventories reduced and physical infrastructure treated as somebody else's problem.
AI is beginning to challenge some of that logic.
Data centers will have over $7 billion invested in them by 2030. You've already seen them become more energy efficient when the newest models have switched from air cooling to liquid cooling, reducing energy use 27%. I argued in _[The Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/ed07a663-992e-4204-8021-910f5bd57409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ that Governor Shapiro has gotten the data center construction policy right by mandating his GRID protections, including bringing their own energy and local approval.
That is not simply a technology story. It is an infrastructure and capital story.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9050740b-a0cd-4c45-a7e2-8fc3ac4e1219?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
AI needs advanced semiconductors, and those chips require fabs, equipment, materials and enormous amounts of capital. Data centers need land, electricity, transmission, transformers, cooling systems, secure networks and skilled workers. The energy needed to support those facilities has to be generated somewhere, transported somehow and connected to infrastructure that can take years to permit and build.
That means the AI competition with China isn't simply about who develops the best model. It is becoming an energy competition, an infrastructure competition, a manufacturing competition and ultimately an industrial-capacity competition.
Some of the most consequential investments of the AI era may therefore have very little to do with building the next model. They may be in the businesses that make the models possible.
America also has to confront a difficult contradiction. We want to lead the world in artificial intelligence, but communities have legitimate concerns about the data centers, power generation and infrastructure required to support it. Questions about electricity prices, water, land and who bears the cost of new infrastructure cannot simply be dismissed in the name of technological competition. There is also evidence of foreign actors trying to exploit that debate. X recently identified roughly [200 accounts linked to a suspected Chinese bot network](https://substack.com/redirect/c6e0cbef-16d0-4fbc-8f6c-702c4d8b3919?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that were posting content designed to influence American arguments over AI and energy policy.
Those concerns are now becoming political. Data-center development and the cost of electricity are increasingly part of the midterm conversation at precisely the moment when the United States is competing with China over AI leadership. That creates a challenge that is both political and strategic: we have to find a way to build the infrastructure required to compete while making sure the communities being asked to host it see real economic benefits to include clean power investment.
It is difficult to imagine America leading the next technological revolution if we cannot figure out how to build the physical infrastructure that powers it.
## **When Washington Finds a Vulnerability, Investors Should Pay Attention**
For investors, this is where the national-security conversation becomes particularly interesting.
When Washington identifies a strategic vulnerability, financial markets have traditionally tended to treat the response primarily as a policy story. I think investors should increasingly ask a different question: is Washington actually identifying a future supply constraint?
Semiconductors show why.
The United States once manufactured close to 40% of the world's semiconductors. By the beginning of this decade, that figure had fallen to roughly 10%. After pandemic-era shortages exposed the consequences of that dependence, Congress responded on a bipartisan basis with the CHIPS and Science Act.
But the number investors should pay attention to isn't simply the roughly $39 billion Congress provided in manufacturing incentives. By early 2025, semiconductor and electronics companies had announced nearly $450 billion in U.S. private investment, according to the Commerce Department.
The significance for investors wasn't simply the federal spending. It was what that spending represented: Washington had identified semiconductor capacity as something the United States could no longer afford to treat as somebody else's problem, and private capital responded at a much larger scale.
The same pattern is appearing elsewhere. The Pentagon created the Office of Strategic Capital to connect private capital with technologies and supply chains important to national security. NATO is asking its members to expand industrial capacity. JPMorganChase has launched a [$1.5 trillion](https://substack.com/redirect/7920ca3a-fea1-481b-b72d-04267cc632a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), ten-year Security and Resiliency Initiative covering advanced manufacturing, critical minerals, defense and aerospace, energy resilience and strategic technologies, including up to $10 billion of direct equity and venture-capital investment.
Look at those categories together and something larger starts to emerge.
What Washington calls a strategic vulnerability may increasingly be useful to investors as a map of where the economy lacks capacity. The vulnerabilities tell us what America and its allies cannot produce enough of, where supply is dangerously concentrated, and which pieces of infrastructure are becoming more important faster than we can build them.
There is a risk in taking that argument too far. Resilience can become an excuse for inefficiency, protectionism or government trying to decide which companies deserve to win. Not every supply chain needs to come home, not every strategic concern justifies a subsidy, and not every company with "national security" in its pitch deck is a good investment.
Investors still have to distinguish disciplined companies from undisciplined ones and durable demand from temporary political enthusiasm. The opportunities I find most interesting are where the vulnerability is real, demand exists beyond a single government program, supply cannot be expanded overnight, private customers have reasons to pay for the solution, and the need is likely to survive changes in political leadership.
When those conditions exist together, you are no longer simply making a bet on Washington. You may be looking at a structural market.
## **China Understood the Value of Industrial Capacity**
China makes this question particularly urgent because it has spent decades building positions not just in finished products, but in the processing and manufacturing layers underneath them.
Rare earths are a striking example. China accounted for roughly [60%](https://substack.com/redirect/7c2a7f5d-b07d-46ae-96ae-a27f2dbbeeb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of global mined production of magnet rare earths in 2024, but mining isn't the most important number. China controlled about 91% of global refining and 94% of permanent-magnet production. In graphite, another strategically important material, China accounted for more than 90% of refining.
Those numbers illustrate why industrial capacity matters.
A country does not need to possess every raw material in the ground to exercise economic leverage if it dominates the point in the supply chain where that raw material becomes useful. And despite the enormous attention now being paid to diversification, the International Energy Agency projects that China could still supply roughly 80% of refined battery-grade graphite and rare earth elements in 2035.
The American answer should not be to imitate China's economic system. Our advantage comes from something very different: the extraordinary ability of American entrepreneurs, workers, universities, capital markets and businesses to move when incentives and national needs begin to align.
Nor should the answer be economic isolation.
America cannot and should not manufacture every product, process every mineral and build every component inside our own borders. Trying to do so would sacrifice many of the enormous benefits of trade without necessarily making the country more secure.
The better objective is strategic capacity: understanding what we absolutely need to control, where we cannot tolerate a single point of failure, which capabilities should be built with trusted partners, and where global markets continue to make us stronger.
## **Reshoring May Be the Wrong Word**
That brings me to North America.
We talk a lot about "reshoring," but I suspect we may eventually look back and realize that reshoring was too narrow a word for what was happening. The larger opportunity may be regionalization.
The scale is already enormous. U.S. goods and services trade with Canada and Mexico totaled more than $1.8 trillion in 2024. Tens of thousands of American small and medium-sized businesses already export to our two neighbors.
Taken together, the United States, Canada and Mexico represent an economy of roughly $35 trillion and a market of more than half a billion people. That is not a small regional trading arrangement. It is an economic platform.
North America also possesses an extraordinary combination of energy, natural resources, advanced manufacturing, technology, capital, workers and consumers. USMCA 1.0 passed in the first Trump Administration already uses rules of origin to encourage more continental production, including a requirement that 75% of a vehicle's content originate in North America to receive preferential tariff treatment.
For investors, that opens a much larger question than which factories come back to Ohio, Pennsylvania or Michigan. The more interesting question is which supply chains can be rebuilt across the continent, where American capital and technology can combine with Canadian resources and Mexican manufacturing capacity, and which businesses will benefit if proximity, energy security and reliable market access become more valuable over the next decade.
The important economic unit of the coming decade may not always be the United States by itself. In some of the industries that matter most, it may increasingly be North America.
That is also why I remain concerned about Congress taking a backseat in the tariff debate, particularly when it comes to Canada. If the strategic objective is to build more resilient supply chains with reliable partners, our trade policy should reinforce that objective rather than work against it.
As I argued recently in writing about the [Constitution as a national-security asset](https://substack.com/redirect/26461666-3bae-470f-8ab8-ef787633ad2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the durability of American policy matters. Investors and allies need to understand not simply what American policy is today, but whether the commitments and rules underlying it can survive changes in administrations and political leadership. Congress has an important constitutional role in providing that durability, particularly when it comes to trade.
There is a difference between dependence on a strategic competitor and interdependence with a strategic partner. Our trade policy should be sophisticated enough to recognize it.
## **Private Capital Is an American Strategic Advantage**
For much of my career in national security, we talked about a "whole-of-government" approach. Looking at the scale of the competition ahead, I increasingly believe that framework is too small.
We need a "whole-of-nation" approach, and private capital has a much larger role in it than we sometimes acknowledge.
One of my mentors, General Colin Powell, understood that American power has never come from the military alone which is why he went from the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff to Secretary of State. Our economy, alliances, institutions and ability to mobilize people and resources are all part of what makes American leadership possible. That lesson feels particularly relevant now.
Look at where the money is already moving. Nearly [$450 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/31f74a6c-a7c4-4fa5-97df-3a35ed9e2df9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in announced private semiconductor and electronics investment followed America's decision to rebuild domestic chip capacity. JPMorganChase alone has committed to facilitate, finance and invest $1.5 trillion over ten years in industries it considers important to economic security and resilience. NATO's new commitment potentially directs another 1.5% of member GDP toward infrastructure, networks, resilience, innovation and industrial capacity on top of traditional defense spending.
Those are not three unrelated developments. They are evidence of a much larger repricing underway.
Government can identify strategic needs, invest in basic research, create demand and remove barriers. Entrepreneurs can develop technologies and build companies around them. Universities can produce breakthroughs and train the workforce. Our allies can expand our collective industrial capacity. But none of those pieces will be enough if promising companies cannot get the capital necessary to scale.
I spent much of my career thinking about American power in military terms. Serving in Iraq will do that. Working at the Pentagon will too. But the longer I have spent in business at Wharton, in boardrooms and as an investor, the more convinced I have become that one of America's greatest strategic advantages isn't sitting inside the Pentagon at all.
It is sitting in rooms like the one I spoke to this week.
The United States has extraordinary pools of private capital connected to an entrepreneurial culture that our strategic competitors cannot easily replicate. The question is whether we can connect enough of that capital to the things the country and our allies are actually going to need.
That isn't charity, and it isn't patriotism masquerading as an investment thesis. These investments still have to generate returns. But some of the most interesting opportunities are created when structural demand is rising and supply has not yet caught up. Geopolitics is now revealing some of those gaps in unusually clear ways.
## **Where Capital Goes Next**
Put all of this together and the scale of the shift becomes easier to see.
Data centers could consume over [$7 trillion in investment before 2030](https://substack.com/redirect/6404b3a9-5254-4eec-9b4f-cbca80542700?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Nearly $450 billion in private semiconductor and electronics investment has already been announced. NATO allies are moving toward a defense and security commitment equal to 5% of GDP. One of America's largest banks is putting a $1.5 trillion financing framework around security and resilience. North America's three economies already trade more than $1.8 trillion in goods and services with one another each year. And China still controls more than 90% of the refining or processing of several materials essential to advanced technology and national defense.
These are not disconnected statistics. They are different manifestations of the same economic change.
Administrations will change. Policies will change. Markets will move. But America will still need more electricity, stronger infrastructure, advanced semiconductors, critical minerals, secure digital networks, manufacturing capacity and a defense industrial base capable of responding when circumstances change. Our allies will need many of the same things.
For most of the last generation, the great investment question was where capital could find the greatest efficiency. That question still matters. Cost, scale, margins and growth have not suddenly become irrelevant.
But the next decade adds another question: where has the pursuit of efficiency created vulnerabilities that the world's largest economies can no longer afford?
That is where I would be looking.
Cheap globalization isn't over because America is retreating from the world. It is ending because geopolitical risk, industrial capacity and reliability can no longer be treated as free.
The next great growth story will still be global. But it will increasingly depend on physical capacity, reliable partners and supply chains capable of surviving a world that is considerably less predictable than the one investors grew accustomed to.
America enters that competition with enormous advantages. We have deep capital markets, extraordinary entrepreneurs, talented workers, world-class research institutions, abundant resources and allies that dramatically expand our economic reach. Most importantly, we have a long history of building quickly when the need becomes clear.
The challenge is getting those strengths to work together.
For the people in the room at SuperReturn, that creates both a responsibility and an opportunity. Private capital will not merely react to this transformation. It will help determine how quickly America can build the energy, infrastructure, technology and industrial capacity the next era requires.
For decades, we became very good at financing efficiency. We now have an opportunity to do something equally consequential: finance the capacity America and our allies can no longer afford to live without.
If we get that right, resilience will not simply protect us from the next crisis. It can become one of America's great competitive advantages.

Goods moved easily across borders, capital followed opportunity, and supply chains stretched across oceans with remarkably little friction. If a component could be manufactured more cheaply somewhere else, that was usually taken as evidence that the system was doing its job. For a long time, it did. But the assumptions underneath that system have become harder to take for granted. Wars have disrupted shipping routes that once seemed dependable. Cyberattacks have demonstrated that infrastructure thousands of miles from a battlefield can become part of the conflict. A shortage of a single component can stop an entire production line. And China's rise has turned semiconductors, energy, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing and artificial intelligence from ordinary commercial considerations into questions of great-power competition. Consider the Strait of Hormuz. Roughly 20.9 million barrels of oil a day moved through it in the first half of 2025, equivalent to about 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption and roughly one-quarter of the world's seaborne oil trade. Yet the available pipelines capable of bypassing the strait could handle only a fraction of that volume. One narrow waterway is a reminder of how much of the global economy still depends on physical infrastructure that investors largely take for granted until something goes wrong. The political response to these vulnerabilities is already reshaping the economic landscape. The Trump administration has put tariffs, domestic manufacturing and economic security at the center of its trade agenda, while treating dependence in areas such as semiconductors and critical minerals as a strategic vulnerability. President Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping later this month, with technology and artificial intelligence among the major issues hanging over the relationship. At home, data centers themselves are becoming a political issue as Americans head toward the midterm elections. Taken together, these debates are forcing a question that business leaders and investors could once largely avoid: what does America actually need to be able to build for itself, and what can we safely rely on others to provide? A factory thousands of miles away may still offer the cheapest unit price, but the calculation changes when the product has to travel through a vulnerable shipping route, when a critical input is controlled by a strategic competitor, or when production cannot be replaced quickly during a crisis. Efficiency still matters. It always will. What has changed is that resilience now has an economic value, and markets are beginning to put a price on it. Today, it belongs much closer to the beginning of the investment memo. | | ---|---|--- The question for investors is no longer simply where capital can find the greatest efficiency. It is where the vulnerabilities of the global economy are beginning to create scarcity, durable demand and, ultimately, opportunity. Those experiences have convinced me that we have spent too much time treating economic capacity and national power as separate subjects. There is an old Pentagon saying that amateurs talk strategy and professionals talk logistics. Like most military aphorisms, it has lasted because reality keeps proving it right. The United States can develop the most sophisticated weapons system in the world, but its strategic value changes considerably if we cannot replace its parts, replenish ammunition, move equipment where it needs to go or increase production during a crisis. If one obscure component buried deep in the supply chain comes from a country we may not be able to rely upon during a conflict, that dependency matters whether or not anyone noticed it on a spreadsheet five years earlier. Our allies have reached much the same conclusion. NATO's new defense investment commitment calls for allies to reach annually by 2035, with at least 3.5% devoted to core defense and up to another 1.5% for critical infrastructure, networks, civil preparedness, resilience, innovation and the defense industrial base. European allies and Canada increased combined defense expenditures by nearly 20% in real terms in 2025. That is a significant amount of capital moving toward capacity, and it reflects a broader realization that national security is no longer principally about buying more weapons. It is also about having the factories, infrastructure, technology, logistics and supply chains necessary to produce and sustain them. The private sector is discovering versions of the same lesson. We saw it when automakers had vehicles sitting unfinished because they could not get enough semiconductors. We see it when utilities wait for transformers and other critical equipment. A supply chain can be extraordinarily efficient until the moment it stops working. That is why investors increasingly need to understand logistics, industrial capacity and geopolitical exposure as part of the investment thesis rather than as risks to be considered after it. Data centers will have over $7 billion invested in them by 2030. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The most important thing I ever did as a state senator wasn't a bill I passed. It was a bill I helped stop. Over and over again.
For all four years I served in the North Carolina Senate, Republicans never once overrode a veto from Governor Roy Cooper. **Not once.** In a legislature where they had the numbers to jam through almost anything, that veto line was the last thing standing between North Carolina and a flood of horrible bills. And we held the line **every single time.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here's what that actually took, because it's not what most people think. Holding the line wasn't about speeches on the floor. It was about the private conversations nobody saw, keeping every Democrat together, vote after vote, when the pressure to peel off just one of us was enormous. There were real fights inside our democratic caucus. More times than I can count, I was the one in the room trying to hold us together, talking it through, finding common ground, reminding everyone what was at stake if just one of us bailed. That kind of unity doesn't happen by accident. Someone has to do the quiet work to make it happen.
I'm telling you this because I know, better than most, what North Carolina gains when a governor has a real veto, and what we lose when he doesn't.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I've known Josh Stein a long time. When I ran for the state Senate in 2018, Josh got behind me early, before I'd ever held office or cast a single vote. He believed in me from the start, and I've never forgotten it. Since then I've watched him serve North Carolina the right way, first as an Attorney General who took on opioid companies and scammers preying on seniors, and now as a governor who shows up, tells the truth, and fights for working families every single day. He's the real deal, and he deserves a real chance to lead.
Right now, Governor Stein doesn't really have the seat at the table. The Republican gerrymandered legislature has the votes to override his vetoes and force their agenda into law, and they've done it again and again. Every time, North Carolina pays for it: dirtier air and water, money drained from our public schools into private vouchers, new barriers to the ballot box and politicians inserting themselves into women's health care decisions.
Think about how different this state will look when Josh has a real seat at the table.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8ed22d6a-9144-45b4-b582-1b41593004f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When a governor's veto actually holds, everything changes. Republicans can't just ram through bills on a party-line vote. They have to come to the table. They have to negotiate. They have to write laws that a majority of North Carolinians can actually live with, instead of the most extreme version their caucus can pass at midnight. A real veto doesn't just stop bad bills. It forces good-faith compromise, and it produces better public policy for everyone, Democrats, Republicans, and unaffiliateds alike. That's how divided government is supposed to work. That's what we had under Roy Cooper, and it's what Josh Stein deserves.
We're not far away. It comes down to just a small number of legislative seats where we have a fair fight. Flip them, and Josh Stein gets his veto, his seat at the table, and the leverage to make this legislature do what's right for North Carolina.
The guy leading that fight in the state House is Democratic Leader Robert Reives. His job is to flip red seats blue. If he does that the governor's veto means something again.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So I'm asking you to help. I've set up a split donation between Robert Reives and me. [Your contribution](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is divided evenly, and goes toward giving Josh Stein the veto he needs and the bipartisan legislation we all deserve.
**[CHIP IN -- SPLIT BETWEEN ROBERT REIVES AND WILEY NICKEL ->](https://substack.com/redirect/fd28331f-60b8-4645-b362-54eff2db5aec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Now let's give Josh Stein a real veto, and give North Carolinians a government that actually has to work together.
Thanks for being in this fight. It matters more than it ever has.
Back to work.
**-- Wiley**

Over and over again. For all four years I served in the North Carolina Senate, Republicans never once overrode a veto from Governor Roy Cooper. Not once. In a legislature where they had the numbers to jam through almost anything, that veto line was the last thing standing between North Carolina and a flood of horrible bills. And we held the line every single time. | | ---|---|--- Here's what that actually took, because it's not what most people think. Holding the line wasn't about speeches on the floor. It was about the private conversations nobody saw, keeping every Democrat together, vote after vote, when the pressure to peel off just one of us was enormous. There were real fights inside our democratic caucus. More times than I can count, I was the one in the room trying to hold us together, talking it through, finding common ground, reminding everyone what was at stake if just one of us bailed. That kind of unity doesn't happen by accident. Someone has to do the quiet work to make it happen. I'm telling you this because I know, better than most, what North Carolina gains when a governor has a real veto, and what we lose when he doesn't. | | ---|---|--- I've known Josh Stein a long time. When I ran for the state Senate in 2018, Josh got behind me early, before I'd ever held office or cast a single vote. He believed in me from the start, and I've never forgotten it. Since then I've watched him serve North Carolina the right way, first as an Attorney General who took on opioid companies and scammers preying on seniors, and now as a governor who shows up, tells the truth, and fights for working families every single day. He's the real deal, and he deserves a real chance to lead. Right now, Governor Stein doesn't really have the seat at the table. The Republican gerrymandered legislature has the votes to override his vetoes and force their agenda into law, and they've done it again and again. Every time, North Carolina pays for it: dirtier air and water, money drained from our public schools into private vouchers, new barriers to the ballot box and politicians inserting themselves into women's health care decisions. Think about how different this state will look when Josh has a real seat at the table. | | ---|---|--- When a governor's veto actually holds, everything changes. Republicans can't just ram through bills on a party-line vote. They have to come to the table. They have to negotiate. They have to write laws that a majority of North Carolinians can actually live with, instead of the most extreme version their caucus can pass at midnight. A real veto doesn't just stop bad bills. It forces good-faith compromise, and it produces better public policy for everyone, Democrats, Republicans, and unaffiliateds alike. That's how divided government is supposed to work. # Make Your Voice Heard on Federal Vaccine Policy
| |
---
|
---
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is asking for public input on the actions outlined in the August 10 Executive Order regarding federal vaccine recommendations and the importance of individualized decision-making. **The public comment window closes September 20, so now is the time to make your voice heard.** This is an opportunity for Texans to tell federal policymakers **what vaccine policy should look like.** Your comment can address the importance of individual autonomy and parental authority, the quality and strength of the evidence behind vaccine recommendations, how shared clinical decision-making should work, and the need for transparency and rebuilding of public trust. **Those same principles are at the heart of TFVC’s work here in Texas.** As we’ve emphasized, however, _proposed_ federal policies do not change Texas law. Texans can still face vaccine requirements affecting education, employment, healthcare, and other areas of life. This is why **TFVC remains focused on ending all remaining allowable vaccine mandates** in the upcoming Texas Legislative Session. **Submit your public comment before September 20 and tell HHS that medical decisions should remain with patients and parents.**

I've met thousands of people in the district, and almost all have been polite, respectful, and supportive. ALMOST ALL...
I met a man in LaFayette and told him I was running for Congress. We talked, and he said he liked what I was saying, especially that I wanted to help LaFayette fix its water system so the water from the faucet didn't run brown. He asked me if I was a Republican. I said no; I'm a Democrat. He looked at me and said he would never vote for me. "Why not?" I asked. He said, "It's the gay thing. You Democrats talk too much about the gays."
I'm running to represent that man.
There was a woman in Roanoke. She told me Chuck Schumer was evil. She said not only was Barack Obama evil, but he was also a Muslim. She told me if I was a Democrat, I was evil.
Yeah, I'm running to represent her.
Even if I wanted to help only the people who voted for me, I couldn't. We can't just help Democrats earn a living wage. That's not how the economy works. We can't just help the people who voted for me get better healthcare. We can't just help the children of Democrats have better schools. # One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
This week, we paused to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks. The memory of that trauma is difficult for many, but we need to remember that the trauma did not end that day.

First responders who selflessly worked "The Pile," searching for survivors and clearing the site, are still suffering from illnesses linked to that work. The wars that followed in response to those attacks have left many coping with injuries that are both seen and unseen.
As a disabled veteran, I have some understanding of the cost these great people are still paying for their service to the United States, and I state without hesitation that I will fight so that they all receive the honors and care they deserve.
It's 49 days until the general election on November 3rd.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

A few years ago, if you said an avowed socialist could be leading the Senate race in Texas, I'd have called you crazy. It's happening. ❌ White men are the greatest domestic terrorist threat in this country❌ God is "non-binary"
❌ The Bible is pro-abortion
❌ Christianity is "the most violent religion"
❌ There are six genders, not two That's not a caricature. That's the man in his own words. Strip away the "Christian" branding, and the policy agenda underneath is standard-issue far left: open borders, government-run healthcare, abortion up to birth, gun control, welfare for illegal immigrants, and a war on parental rights in schools.
And Texas isn't the only place this is happening. In Florida, DSA candidate Angie Nixon just won her primary by 12 points. In Oklahoma, DSA candidate N'Kiyla "Jasmine" Thomas won hers by 22. If either candidate wins in November, they'd be the first Democratic socialists ever elected to the U.S. Senate. And let's be honest. Socialist is their label meant to soften what they truly are **—** Marxists. **This rise of full-blown Communism isn't a fringe problem in blue states. It's on the ballot in Florida, Oklahoma, and Texas — deep-red states — this November.** So who stops it? Not the Republican establishment. Not the DC insiders. It has to be true conservative fighters. This is fantastic news. But before we go giving the most corrupt, partisan court in American history too much credit, this ruling has a major "for now" caveat.
In his concurring opinion, MAGA Justice Brett Kavanaugh said that the USPS rule had at least a fair prospect of falling within their authority, but applying the rule in the 2026 elections would be a violation of the Administrative Procedure Act because state election officials do not have sufficient time to implement the rule before the election.
In other words, they did not rule on whether the rule itself was constitutional, only on its timing. That means it could resurface again before the 2028 election, and the MAGA occupied court could very well let it happen.
Trump's response to the news was just as you'd expect. In a long, barely coherent rant on "Truth" Social, he flamed the justices, saying that "these are not the justices I interviewed" and admitted that this was a "big loss for Republicans."

name: Dr. Karl Morris
subject: A Postmortem and Our New AI Future
body:
[](https://karlforcongress.us/updates/29199f99/)
---
On May 19, 2026, the Democratic Party held its primary elections to select its representative for Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. Unfortunately, after months of meeting with voters, speaking to community groups, and sharing my vision that Washington desperately needs technical literacy, our campaign was unsuccessful. In fact, we did not even make it to the ballot, having been knocked off by a Democratic party challenge and an unsuccessful Pennsylvania Supreme Court appeal. To everyone who supported us throughout this journey and reached out after the news (and to those who wrote my name in): thank you. A [22% voter turnout](https://philadelphiaresults.azurewebsites.us/VoterTurnoutDetails.aspx) is not an accident; it's the predictable outcome of a Democratic machine prioritizing self-preservation over voter choice. In the end, however, the buck stopped with me. I failed to rally support to prepare for the impending threat of artificial intelligence run amok. The heavier loss isn't electoral, though; it's what comes next.
#### It's Much Worse Than We Imagined
The unfortunate result of this past election is that the status quo in Congress will continue. With no expertise or leadership in artificial intelligence, the technology will continue to change every facet of our lives without any meaningful guardrails or regulation. Our failure to act will leave us at the mercy of a handful of tech trillionaires, and, eventually, the technology itself. In my 16 years as a computer scientist working with AI, I have always been aware of its potential to restructure the economy and rewrite the rules of our society. What I did not anticipate was the speed with which we'd get here. In just a few short years, AI moved from science fiction to [displacing jobs](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6aa833b1/ " AI Job Displacement Statistics 2026: What the Data Actually Shows \(and What It Doesn’t\)") and sparking discussions about [human extinction](https://link.karlforcongress.us/6aa832ee/ "AI could kill all humans in next decade, warn experts: but how seriously should we take them?"). We have entered an era where the threat posed by AI can no longer be ignored, yet leaders in Washington have no idea what to do about it. I am not giving up. This moment is too important, and if we miss it, we may not get another. I will continue speaking out to make it clear what's at stake and equip citizens with the information they need to demand change from their elected officials. My hope is that a grassroots effort will bring about the needed shift in Washington to mitigate the harms that we as a society are about to face. We cannot simply watch from the sidelines. The fight doesn't end with this election; this is where it starts!

**Tuesday, September 15, 2026**
In the rainy season, the earth possesses a relentless memory, surging back the very overgrowth you have just cleared. The mower is back out, and with it, the peculiar frustration of a task that refuses to stay finished. It is a wearying thing to fight a battle against the grass, especially when the machinery of the world seems designed to wear a man down.
As I push the mower forward, I see the goats and cattle on the horizon. They are grateful for that which has become a bother to me, and I feel a humbling irony, that my burden is their feast.
There is a hidden peace in the rhythm of the rain. The work does not stop, but neither do we. That is where our endurance is built.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Now, Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

The mower is back out, and with it, the peculiar frustration of a task that refuses to stay finished. It is a wearying thing to fight a battle against the grass, especially when the machinery of the world seems designed to wear a man down. As I push the mower forward, I see the goats and cattle on the horizon. They are grateful for that which has become a bother to me, and I feel a humbling irony, that my burden is their feast. There is a hidden peace in the rhythm of the rain. The work does not stop, but neither do we. That is where our endurance is built. Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper. Now, Refuel. Welcome to Sweet Ground. Since then, he’s not only occupied the White House — he’s occupied every American’s head rent-free. Trump believes that the presidency should guarantee him absolute power over our country and its citizens, and his MAGA allies continue to indulge his delusions. Republican governors and members of Congress have rubber-stamped his disastrous agenda to start endless wars, cut funding for federal agencies, and shutter rural hospitals. And hardworking Americans have been stuck with the bill. This November is a chance to deliver a real check to Trump’s egomania. That’s why we’re launching our NO RUBBER STAMPS FUND today. Our goal is to raise $200,000 over the next three days to elect the Democratic pro-choice women who will take back power and flip Republican-held seats across the country. = | = Republicans have had two years to stand up to Trump — but they’ve spent their time disappointing their communities instead. | | From childhood, Kaillie Armbruster Humphries dreamed of becoming an Olympian. She didn’t just achieve that dream, she became the most accomplished woman in bobsledding history, winning six Olympic medals and numerous World Championship titles. But there was another dream in Kaillie’s heart: becoming a mother. When she was told she would have to put that dream aside, Kaillie did what champions do. She refused to give up. Kaillie joins us to share her remarkable journey from competing for Canada to making history with Team USA as the first woman to win Olympic gold in monobob. But beyond the medals and championships, she’ll talk about a victory she considers even more meaningful: becoming a mom. It’s a story of perseverance, courage, and refusing to let someone else tell you which dreams are worth pursuing. Full episode available now on [YouTube](https://momsforamerica.us/so/caQ2bQLNH/c?w=DJ1Sk71CUOTBlOYUgMZsxmAbjgpPsSY-pRPB1y0yYMg.), [Rumble](https://momsforamerica.us/so/caQ2bQLNH/c?w=z09epRBz4IPtfIKX4Yykm8I_CdP9GV6sMhFcwj4jWZY.), [Spotify](https://momsforamerica.us/so/caQ2bQLNH/c?w=AJQEiqF3o3nIn6G5rTf87_Bz0Q7oNfJ9VdZd9JMe6O4.), and [Apple](https://momsforamerica.us/so/caQ2bQLNH/c?w=-7as9WoU6B4dFnD-Eu2XsRuzB8GoPm7H-_8vxB9q3_s.).

| | For too long, women and girls have been told to surrender fairness, privacy, and safety in the name of “inclusion.” But protecting women’s sports and private spaces is not hateful. It is common sense. WNBA star Sophie Cunningham recently said what too few women in professional sports are willing to say: girls deserve to compete against girls, and women’s rights deserve protection. And she isn’t alone. Roughly 80% of Americans agree that men should not compete in women’s sports. Women should not have to apologize for defending boundaries that exist to protect them. We can love our neighbors while still telling the truth about biological reality and standing firmly for women and girls. It’s time to cut the crazy, stand up for our girls, and protect what women fought so hard to achieve. clean_body: Cut The Crazy - No More Men in Women's Sports & Spaces | | Can 't see this message? | | | | | | September 15, 2026 Newsletter | | Finding Gold in the Olympics and in Motherhood | | | From childhood, Kaillie Armbruster Humphries dreamed of becoming an Olympian. She didn’t just achieve that dream, she became the most accomplished woman in bobsledding history, winning six Olympic medals and numerous World Championship titles. But there was another dream in Kaillie’s heart: becoming a mother. When she was told she would have to put that dream aside, Kaillie did what champions do. She refused to give up. Kaillie joins us to share her remarkable journey from competing for Canada to making history with Team USA as the first woman to win Olympic gold in monobob. But beyond the medals and championships, she’ll talk about a victory she considers even more meaningful: becoming a mom. It’s a story of perseverance, courage, and refusing to let someone else tell you which dreams are worth pursuing. Full episode available now on , , , and . | | | | | | Cut The Crazy - No More Men in Women's Sports & Spaces | | | For too long, women and girls have been told to surrender fairness, privacy, and safety in the name of “inclusion.” But protecting women’s sports and private spaces is not hateful. It is common sense. WNBA star Sophie Cunningham recently said what too few women in professional sports are willing to say: girls deserve to compete against girls, and women’s rights deserve protection. And she isn’t alone. Roughly 80% of Americans agree that men should not compete in women’s sports. Women should not have to apologize for defending boundaries that exist to protect them. We can love our neighbors while still telling the truth about biological reality and standing firmly for women and girls. It’s time to cut the crazy, stand up for our girls, and protect what women fought so hard to achieve. # Patriot,
---
There's now a law in California with my name associated with it. Everyone in Sacramento knows exactly what the **"Stop Nick Shirley Act"** means. On August 22nd, Governor Newsom signed AB 2624. Three days later, I was standing at the State Capitol with a crowd of people who showed up because they understood what this law _actually_ does.
---
[](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)
---
Supporters say it protects immigration workers from harassment. Here's what it really does, Patriot: **it makes it harder for anyone — me included — to investigate where your tax dollars are being sent.** I said it plainly at the rally: this is not the end; _this is just the beginning._ Because here's the part that should bother you more than anything else. **The assemblymember who wrote this bill is married to California's Attorney General** — the _one person_ in this state whose entire job is supposed to be going after fraud. Instead, his wife wrote the bill that makes it harder to expose it. That's not a coincidence, Patriot. That's the system protecting itself. **[Patriot, will you make a tax-deductible gift of $25, $50, or $100 today to help keep independent journalists like me in the field?](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)**
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Help Keep Independent Journalists in the Field** ](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)
---
I've spent the last year showing up where legacy media won't — daycare centers, tax-funded nonprofits, the offices of people who'd rather I disappear than answer a question. That work is exactly why a state legislature decided to write a law with my name on it instead of going after the fraud I keep finding. A state senator at the rally called it unconstitutional. A city attorney called it a direct threat to the First Amendment. _They're right_ — and they're not going to be the ones who stop it. That's going to take people willing to fund the reporters still asking the questions. Here's something most people don't see, Patriot: doing this work independently means there's no network paying for the flight to Sacramento, no legal department covering me if a state files a complaint over a story, no corporate budget for the cameras and editors it takes to get this footage in front of you. When I showed up at that rally, **Lincoln Media Foundation** was on site with their own journalists to cover it, because they understood what was actually at stake before most of the country did. _That’s why I’m partnering with Lincoln Media Foundation._ They understand how important it is to support independent journalists and help us keep doing the work without compromising what makes it independent in the _first place._ I’m grateful for their partnership and commitment, and **[every dollar you give to LMF goes directly toward keeping reporters like me in the field](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)** – helping cover travel, equipment, and the costs that come with confronting people on camera instead of reading a press release about them.

**Since LMF is a 501(c)3, your gift is tax-deductible** , and it can be made anonymously if that's what you'd prefer.
---
[ **Yes —****I'll****Fund Independent Investigations** ](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)
---
Patriot, they can pass all the laws they want. They can try to prevent people like me from exposing their corruption, that’s why it crucial to support independent journalists like myself. They are creating laws to silence free speech — and that’s why we need to continue the fight and I need your support. People like you decide this work is worth funding, and it helps me continue! **[Will you help LMF keep me — and journalists like me — in the field with a gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can give today?](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)**
---
For the truth,

_**Nick Shirley**_
---
[ **Help Support Nick’s Work** ](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)
---
P.S. — A California assemblyman is already asking the DOJ to intervene against this law. That tells you how serious this is. **[A tax-deductible gift today helps LMF keep me and other independent journalists in the field while this fight plays out.](https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.)**

body:

| [](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjUwMDB9AAwAAAAAAvhtOf9Fe-nIHPWX8UsyvMK1qG3NbjYdaMLbjC0JAOSB7-9O0A9-6s2ZE_eU8iiwNQ34iP6gldAHHkclUACq7Ic-X23GNeWro2Xqa6uh)
Fellow Concerned American,

Parents send their kids to school to learn reading, writing, and math... not to receive anatomically explicit toys with removable body parts from school staff.

But that’s exactly what might be coming to Minnesota schools soon.

**Fox News reported that “MyGender Dolls” will be available to school counselors, educators, and clinicians this school year.**

These “trans” dolls were developed through the University of Minnesota’s Early Innovation Fund, under a program Gov. Tim Walz has championed and been personally honored for. _They ship with removable, swappable genitalia and are built for children**ages 4-10**_.

And it gets worse...

Not a single Minnesota parent that Defending Education spoke with had received any notification about the dolls. **_There is no confirmed way to opt out_**.

That’s why Defending Education filed a federal privacy complaint – citing violations of the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment, and the First and Fourteenth Amendments.

I’m Nicole Neily, President of **Defending Education** – a national grassroots organization fighting to restore academic excellence and parental rights in America’s schools.

We believe four-year-olds have no business handling anatomically explicit material from any adult, in any building, for any reason. **We believe parents – not a governor, not a university lab – decide what’s appropriate for their child.**

And we believe it’s time to ask Americans plainly where they stand.

name: Cody for SC
subject: Thank You for Your Support — 50 Days to Victory!
body:
| | | | | | |

Dear Team,
Thank you for your incredible support, energy, and commitment throughout the primary election. Because of YOU, Team Cody is stronger, more energized, and ready for the road ahead!
Now, the real work continues.
**We are officially 50 days away from Election Day!** **36 days from Early Voting!** Every conversation, phone call, door knocked, and volunteer hour between now and Election Day can make a difference.We are **Team "Win Cody Win** ," and we are ready to finish this race strong. Our goal is simple: build a strong grassroots movement across South Carolina and make sure voters know why **Cody Simpson** is the right choice for **the next South Carolina Commissioner of Agriculture.**

### UPCOMING VOLUNTEER TRAINING
**Volunteer Training Day — Columbia**
**Saturday, September 19th**
**9:00 AM–11:00 AM**
**Rhodes Branding**
[**2628 Millwood Ave**](https://us.list-manage.com/n47qnQfLyxu?e=a062c2be69&c2id=0eeefb4b292ad0ebb90d8335c42ce0cf)
[**Columbia, SC 29205**](https://us.list-manage.com/1AeJCrdhPX0?e=a062c2be69&c2id=0eeefb4b292ad0ebb90d8335c42ce0cf)

Join us for volunteer training this Saturday and learn how you can plug into the campaign, connect with voters, and help us build momentum across the state. For those who are unable to make it to Columbia, we will be hosting a **Zoom training session on Saturday evening at 5:00 PM.**
**Please RSVP**[**Click HERE: RSVP Form**](https://us.list-manage.com/LWT9X4KLL89?e=a062c2be69&c2id=0eeefb4b292ad0ebb90d8335c42ce0cf)**.** If you are unable to attend in person, **please reply to Jordan Snipes, our Volunteer Coordinator, by email at**[**jordansnipesofficial@gmail.com**](mailto:jordansnipesofficial@gmail.com)**or text message at** [**843-9563007**](tel:\(843\)%20956-3007)**** so that we can make arrangements to connect with you another way.
Whether you've volunteered with us before or this will be your first time, **there is a place for you on Team Cody!**
**50 days. One team. One goal. " WIN, CODY, WIN!"**
Thank you again for believing in this campaign and for being part of the movement.Let's WIN together!

Jordan Snipes _**Volunteer Coordinator**_**Join the RUN at codyforsc.com—and encourage your friends and family to join the movement, too.**

This is why I’m backing Gina Hinojosa. And she needs your support too.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260915_1_eva.t9YaA_&refcode=em20260915-2119&amount=5&t=1&akid=2119%2E299639%2E68bOrn)
Hi Peter, Eva Longoria here.
We are officially 49 days away from Election Day, and there are a lot of critical races on the ballot this fall. But the Texas governor’s race is especially important and personal to me, and my friend Gina Hinojosa needs your support right now.
I’ll tell you why I’m so proud to stand with Gina in just a moment, but first: [**Will you make a donation of any amount today to power her campaign for Governor of Texas?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260915_1_eva.t9YaA_&refcode=em20260915-2119&amount=5&t=2&akid=2119%2E299639%2E68bOrn)
Like Gina, I was born and raised in South Texas. I am a proud Texan through and through. **But the Texas that Gina and I grew up in is simply not the Texas our families are living in today.**
We were raised on the American Dream. The core belief that if you work hard, you can buy a home, raise a family, build a career, and live with security. But under Greg Abbott's leadership, that promise has been stripped away.
Because of Greg Abbott, everyday families are stuck paying more and getting less. From his no-bid contracts to his public school voucher scam and massive corporate tax giveaways for his ultra-wealthy friends, hard-working Texans are the ones stuck paying the bill.
**Texans deserve better. We pay for strong public schools, reliable infrastructure, and lower costs, and it is time we actually get what we deserve.** And I know that if we elect Gina this fall, we can make Texas a state where everyone can prosper.
This November, we have a real opportunity to win a better Texas and restore the American Dream for every family. But Gina can’t take on Greg Abbott without our collective support right now.
**[Peter, will you join me and pitch in any amount to Gina’s campaign today to finally bring real, honest leadership back to Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260915_1_eva.t9YaA_&refcode=em20260915-2119&amount=5&t=3&akid=2119%2E299639%2E68bOrn)**

Thank you for being a part of this fight for a better Texas.
— Eva Longoria

Friend, as an emergency medicine physician and lawyer, I know firsthand that emergency abortion care can be life saving when things go wrong with a pregnancy.[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139233568/646697675/241827350?refcode=082926&sourceid=1052158&ms=091526&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNMDEvMS8xMTg5NjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDY5NmJhNjEtMTNiMS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CkmAXoRe3Ao-zEDLRQLoa1ZM3tdfLFVy7j3bgJhcioI=) I also know that my ability to provide care for my patients is contingent upon Virginians’ access to reproductive health care. **That’s why I’m voting YES on 1, an amendment on the ballot that will enshrine reproductive freedom into Virginia’s Constitution.**
---
[ DEFEND REPRO FREEDOM ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139233569/646697676/241827350?refcode=091526&sourceid=1052158&ms=091526&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNMDEvMS8xMTg5NjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDY5NmJhNjEtMTNiMS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CkmAXoRe3Ao-zEDLRQLoa1ZM3tdfLFVy7j3bgJhcioI=)

While some Virginians might see this amendment and think, “Well, I don’t ever plan to have an abortion,” the reality is that they or a loved one could easily have a pregnancy-related complication that requires abortion care, even if they don’t realize it. Right now, the national patchwork of reproductive health care bans and restrictions is making it harder for physicians like me to provide care. In any given state, including ours, the legal landscape can change on a whim with a change in administration. And legal challenges to mifepristone only add to the confusion, even though the abortion pill is also critical for treating miscarriages and preventing complications like hemorrhage and sepsis. **When you vote YES on 1, you’ll be protecting Virginians’ freedom to make deeply personal decisions about birth control, miscarriage management, prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, fertility care, and abortion care into Virginia’s Constitution.** If we fail to pass this amendment and there is a political shift in the future, we could lose access to reproductive healthcare! **[That’s why I urge you to support Virginians for Reproductive Freedom’s historic campaign today by making a contribution that will help fuel our fight to victory on November 3.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139233570/646697677/241827350?refcode=091526&sourceid=1052158&ms=091526&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNMDEvMS8xMTg5NjAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDY5NmJhNjEtMTNiMS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZjFkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=CkmAXoRe3Ao-zEDLRQLoa1ZM3tdfLFVy7j3bgJhcioI=)**

I’ve seen how confusing and frightening it can be when doctors have to worry about whether providing necessary care could lead to jail time or the loss of a medical license. Patients should never have to wonder if politics will get in the way of the care they need. A YES on 1 vote will mean we can keep health care decisions where they belong, _between patients and the medical professionals they trust._ With the future health and well-being of Virginians and our families at stake, please help us spread the word to **Vote YES on 1!**

Derek, the final reporting deadline before voting begins is tonight at midnight. I want to explain why your support is crucial to our success. This is a longer message, but I hope you'll read to the end. You can click [here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139233405/646697266/-1728833127?amount=50&refcode=260915em-deadline&refcode2=260915em-deadline_kaine&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmZmQ0NDBhNS0xMmIxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G6eT22ogTvzDWZ737K1kHouLSAplih_gZ1SNMr3i6v8=) to split a donation between Tim Kaine and my campaign if you're ready to give.

This moment calls for leaders who deliver results, not excuses. **That’s what I’ve done as Senator, and that’s what I will do as Governor.** I have a record of taking on hard fights and winning them. Before I ever held political office, **I took on the insurance companies** \-- and won**.** When our daughter Abigail was born, she was in the ICU. But I was discharged after just 24 hours because of insurance rules. I helped advocate for Minnesota to pass one of the first laws in the country guaranteeing new moms and their babies a 48-hour hospital stay. In the Senate, **I took on Big Pharma** by leading the fight to let Medicare negotiate lower prescription drug prices. And won. **I’ll bring that same energy to governing.** We can reduce premiums, lower prescription drug costs, and protect access to health care and our hospitals and clinics. Welcome to the official _Team Kristi!_ newsletter. _Walk the Walk_ isn't just a slogan on this campaign, it's our daily drive! Let's dive into this past week and see what all happened with our movement to bring real representation for Tennessee's 1st District to Washington!
* * *
### Kristi's on Tour!
The **Walk the Walk District Tour** ramped up this past weekend, with another important stop for Team Kristi in **Sevier County**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/47bfff33-063d-4277-a64f-e8fd0849c9b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Kristi spoke with local voters, amped them up for the upcoming election, and the team got to work door-knocking in the area. That'll be the hallmark of the entire tour: the team will be **walking the walk** and talking to their neighbors all across Tennessee's 1st District!
We've got stops in all 12 counties lined up, including two this week! You can catch Team Kristi in [Cocke County on Thursday, Sept. 17](https://substack.com/redirect/3f899e62-a4e9-40d7-9161-5409e88ec75a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and in [Johnson County on Saturday, Sept. 19](https://substack.com/redirect/6a0d8dbc-3eaf-459a-ae5d-f0f014cbcac8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)!
The best way to keep up with Kristi's tour stops and other campaign events is to sign up for updates on Mobilize! You'll get notifications on your phone for events you've signed up to attend, plus optional updates for other events near you where you can participate and make a difference!
[Sign Up for Mobilize Updates](https://substack.com/redirect/93331fa7-132b-4fd2-937c-1a1fdfadf911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Win the 'Walk the Walk Off' Golden Boot!
Want to get a head-start on door-knocking in your county before the Walk the Walk Tour makes a stop? You don't have to wait! You can sign up to volunteer with the campaign, be assigned a turf in your neighborhood, and start canvassing right now!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a3126e2-2103-485f-b570-4fdd73554fb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Did you know we're doing a competition for our canvassers?! It's the **Walk the Walk Off** , and our top three winners will get dinner with Team Kristi - plus our 1st-place winner will receive the awesome **Golden Boot** trophy!
Don't wait! Join Team Kristi by clicking the button below!
[Sign Up to Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/bbecf430-0723-4601-ba0f-91c5a17ed750?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Sign Waving Events
Team Kristi and our campaign supporters have been out and about for several **sign-waving events** recently! These are great opportunities to come out into the community, join folks who believe in Kristi's movement, and make an impact!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a54d7240-120b-46f6-8751-4c2226261fd0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You never know where a sign-waving event will pop up! Be sure to [check out our Facebook events](https://substack.com/redirect/372db32c-95af-474c-96ea-b641671df4e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or, even better, [sign up for Mobilize updates](https://substack.com/redirect/93331fa7-132b-4fd2-937c-1a1fdfadf911?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/75e8c0ef-b9aa-4f60-ba86-a596ef612fe3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
### Campaign Hits $177K Fundraising Milestone
Since the beginning, this campaign has been run on the idea of better representation for working people in East Tennessee, and we're proud to say that those same working neighbors have put more than $175,000 into this movement. We've now raised over **$177,000** to be exact!!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5dd6734f-b8e4-459c-8209-19968fdf3333?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We could not have done this without the support of everyday, working people who believe in this movement and in what Kristi could bring to Congress.
Around lunchtime today, we're going to be kicking off a 48-hour drive to raise approximately $4,200 by end of day Thursday. This will help us with production costs for our first ad, which we are filming within the coming days!
Want to get a head start and help us get there early? You can chip in right here:
[Chip In Now](https://substack.com/redirect/445c3954-9eba-4cb8-8960-6895227c97c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Get Involved This Week!
Want to learn more and make a difference in your district? Here's a look at some [great opportunities](https://substack.com/redirect/372db32c-95af-474c-96ea-b641671df4e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to meet Kristi and get involved with the **campaign at events this week**!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eb8ea934-262d-4881-a0f1-7df47c0473db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
Don't just watch from the sidelines! We need help with door-knocking, phone-banking, events, and more! Join Team Kristi! Fill out a volunteer application here:
[Volunteer Form](https://substack.com/redirect/bbecf430-0723-4601-ba0f-91c5a17ed750?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
### Want to Make a Big Impact?
As you can see, this movement is everywhere, and it's growing every day. But change doesn't happen without work and real grassroots effort. We could not make this happen without **YOU** , East Tennessee. Will you join the fight? Even a donation of $5 or $10 can make a world of difference.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dfcc8a1c-7cf4-47be-ab58-4d22abb2c1c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Thank you for helping us raise **$5,877.50** this past week! We are so proud to say that this movement is powered by small-dollar donations, and totally free of corporate PAC or AIPAC money! **Our average donation this week was $47.02**! Want to help us celebrate that? You can **give just $25** right now to show you're all in on Kristi for Congress!
[Chip In Now](https://substack.com/redirect/445c3954-9eba-4cb8-8960-6895227c97c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

_Be sure you 're following us on all socials! You can also grab merch, request yard signs, join coalitions, and find all kinds of other goodies on our Linktree._
[See Our Links](https://substack.com/redirect/dac52823-88f4-4fff-81a3-3682137b3b03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We'll see you next week!

name: Caitlin Cattelino
subject: Reminder: Roadless Rule Webinar Wednesday!
body:
Join Defenders public lands experts to learn more about how you can help protect our roadless areas!

Join Defenders public lands experts to learn more about how you can help protect our roadless areas!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6015917/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6015918/38SyG9Xl)

Dear Defender,

I wanted to make sure you saw my last email about joining Defenders' Roadless Rule Webinar tomorrow. If you haven’t signed up yet, there is still time to do so! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6015919/38SyG9Xl)

In August, the Trump administration published its proposal to repeal the Roadless Rule, one of our country’s most important conservation policies. If this rule is rescinded, America’s last remaining intact forests will be opened up to road construction, destructive timber harvest and energy development, despite these conservation areas lacking commercial value.

And our cherished wildlife will also be negatively impacted. Even though roadless areas only make up 2% of land in the lower 48 states, they contain habitat for 57% of vulnerable wildlife, including jaguars in Arizona and Carolina northern flying squirrels in the southern Appalachian Mountains.

The Trump administration is accepting comments from the public through September 21. Join our webinar to learn more about why the Roadless Rule is so important to protect and how to submit your comment urging the administration to NOT repeal it.

Here are the webinar details:

WHAT: Protect the Roadless Rule

WHEN: Wednesday, September 16

TIME: 7:00pm ET / 6:00pm CT / 5:00pm MT / 4:00pm PT

WHERE: Live via Zoom

Register here – a zoom link will be sent to you (https://support.defenders.org/s/6015920/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6015921/38SyG9Xl)

Repealing the Roadless Rule would put hundreds of species at greater risk of extinction, and it would deprive us of some of the last places we can go to experience the natural wonders of American forests that haven’t been carved up by roads.

Wildlife Defenders, like you, have the power to speak up and demand that our forests remain protected for wildlife!

Hope to see you tomorrow! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6015922/38SyG9Xl)

Caitlin Cattelino

Director of National Outreach

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)
