Over the weekend, Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk -- three men who have spent years telling us the race is the point -- all said out loud that somebody needs to slow the race down. When the arsonists start asking for a fire code, you pay attention. The White House called it a Chinese hoax. David Shuster spent this week on what happens next, and the back half of this piece is the part I would pay for: what the people inside that building are quietly telling him to do about it, and why he probably will not. That reporting is for members. -- Cliff by David Shuster In golf, it is a one foot putt. In basketball, it is called a wide-open layup. . In soccer or hockey, it is the shot taken from three feet away at an empty net. Whatever the terminology, Donald Trump now has one of the easiest political plays imaginable sitting in front of him. It is also a matter involving the continued existence of the human race. And yet there is every indication that Trump may find a way to miss. The subject is artificial intelligence. This past weekend, the leading competing titans of the A.I. industry each said A.I. research needs to slow down. | | ---|---|--- Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for governments to "pace" frontier AI development, arguing that capabilities are advancing too quickly for existing safeguards to keep up. Open AI's Sam Altman said he agrees and supports greater coordination. Elon Musk weighed in and said Amodei and Altman are correct and that there needs to be government mandated and enforced restraint. Other prominent AI figures are also advocating for independent safety evaluations and government involvement. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Front line AI researchers have been issuing dire warnings for months. Most recently and prominently, 27-year-old researcher Jacob Coxon quit his job at Anthropic and declared, in a now viral social media post and several interviews, that OpenAI and Anthropic have been working irresponsibly. Coxon declared that people building the technology genuinely believe it could kill everybody by the end of the decade. For a primer on the threats of superintelligence and the key issues, please read this column by my colleague . | | and | | ---|---|--- | Sep 12 | As Lawrence notes, some of the people engaged in this race think the chances are high that it will trigger a human extinction event. The question is no longer whether A.I. will transform civilization. That part is settled. It will. The question is whether civilization will remain in charge of the transformation and live to use it. I believe that A.I. could produce miracles. It may accelerate the conquest of cancer, transform medicine, improve education, increase productivity beyond anything previously imagined, and solve problems that have tortured humankind for centuries. It may someday make the ordinary human workweek look like an eccentric historical curiosity. Great. | | ---|---|--- But do we have to try and reach this paradise by conducting the most consequential technological experiment in human history according to the business philosophy of a Las Vegas casino? Build faster. Deploy faster. Beat the other gambler. And if you lose, oh well. There is always another table. Except in this case, perhaps everybody dies. The sensible proposal is not to ban A.I. Nor is it to strangle technological development or voluntarily hand America's technological lead to Beijing. The sensible proposal is considerably less dramatic: establish rules for the most powerful systems so this is not a race in which nobody can afford to brake. That means independent testing. Reporting requirements. Serious security standards. Restrictions on deploying systems that fail clearly defined safety evaluations. And legal mechanisms permitting competing companies to share certain safety information without being treated as conspirators against the sacred interests of commerce. None of this is exotic or extreme We already regulate banks, airplanes, nuclear reactors, pharmaceuticals and other things that can produce unpleasant consequences when operated carelessly. Civilization has occasionally learned that "move fast and break things" is not an adequate philosophy when the thing being broken happens to be civilization. The central problem is a simple one. | | ---|---|--- Every leading A.I. company may rationally believe that slowing down would be safer. But each company also fears that if it slows down while its competitors continue racing, it will lose the race. So everyone in the A.I. industry accelerates. This is not necessarily because everyone is insane. It is because everyone is responding rationally to an irrational set of incentives involving trillions of dollars in potential revenue. That is precisely the kind of problem government regulations exist to solve. The strongest objection, as Donald Trump has pointed to, involves China. If the U.S. slows down, would Beijing? A unilateral American retreat could surrender an important economic and strategic advantage. And as Trump said recently, "whoever wins the A.I. race wins." | | ---|---|--- But regulation and technological leadership are not opposites. The United States could seek international agreements governing the most dangerous capabilities while continuing to invest aggressively in research, computing, semiconductor manufacturing, robotics, and less hazardous applications. Indeed, American leadership may be more valuable if it produces standards that other countries ultimately adopt. The easiest part of all of this involves U.S. domestic politics. Trump's approval/disapproval rating is now the worst of any U.S. President in fifty years. And in his handling of Artificial Intelligence, a new just found that 23 percent of American voters say Trump has handled AI well, compared with 57 percent who say he has handled it poorly. That's a minus 34. Among independent voters, Trump is at minus 61. | | ---|---|--- According to a poll conducted by CBS News, 54 percent of voters would prefer a candidate who opposes new data centers in their area, compared to 15 percent who would prefer one who supports building them. Even if Americans don't believe A.I. will extinguish humanity, most voters believe AI will bring them financial ruin. The U-Mass poll found 64 percent of Americans think AI will reduce the number of jobs, while just 19 percent say it will create more. There are some Trump White House staff who see the polling, appreciate the dire challenges facing Trump's GOP in the mid-term elections, and also worry about the existential threat that A.I. may pose. These aides have reportedly advised Trump to deliver a prime-time speech to the nation, declare that certain aspects of A.I. could threaten humanity, and announce specific A.I. regulations the industry is requesting. Trump could also claim he is saving humanity from extinction. And in this case, Trump would probably be correct. body:
I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.

| [](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkxNV9UTi1XVS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMjM3NzItMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MTVfVE4tV1UuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDIzNzcyLTI4OTkifQ/bvaw9YRLieaaBRGS__X2PQ)

Peter,
Do you believe in the power of prayer?
My name’s Troy Downing. When America faced its darkest hour after 9/11, I knew I couldn't just sit on the sidelines. I enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and served eight years in a Combat Search and Rescue squadron, deploying twice to Afghanistan.
On those missions, flying into danger to rescue wounded soldiers, you rely on something much bigger than yourself. Through every deployment and dark night, God’s guiding hand was our shield and protection.
Now, as a Member of Congress working to defend the American Dream and protect our GOP Majority, the battlefield has changed, but the spiritual stakes are just as high. I still rely on God’s unchanging, guiding hand every single day.
[If you believe in God and the power of prayer to guide our leaders and protect our land, I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkxNV9UTi1XVS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMjM3NzItMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MTVfVE4tV1UuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDIzNzcyLTI4OTkifQ/Ia0_V9Q5L7bTXqa1FhKoIQ)

name: Roy Cooper
subject: about my decision
body:
I can’t do this alone, Peter.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1338&source=&t=1&akid=3467%2E124072%2Eg0M1JA) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m in a bit of a bind.
A recent poll shows that our race is now statistically tied, and the Senate GOP’s top super PACs are currently outspending us to boost my Republican opponent. That’s because Senate control hinges on this battleground race.
Since I’m running a grassroots campaign, I can’t fight back without you. So if you’re able to chip in a few bucks to power our fight before our mid-month deadline tonight, I’d really appreciate it. Here’s the link to donate:
[**_https:/actblue.com/donate_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1338&amount=5&t=8&akid=3467%2E124072%2Eg0M1JA)
Now, my decision to run for Senate wasn’t made lightly.
Serving as Governor was one of the great experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs to giving school teachers much-needed raises to expanding access to Medicaid, **my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people – and we did that.**
That’s why it’s so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders have turned their backs on hardworking people. Insiders like Michael Whatley, my opponent in this race.
My opponent says he’ll lower costs, but he built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil and utility companies at the expense of working families. He says he’ll protect our communities, but as chair of the state GOP, he appointed a convicted child sex offender who served six years in prison to powerful leadership roles within the party because he could raise money. He claims he’ll fight for North Carolinians, but it’s clear that **_his_ priority is choosing himself and his wealthy friends.**
_It’s no wonder why the President anointed him to run after Thom Tillis bowed out of running for this seat._
So while I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut resources for public education and chip away at the middle class. They are not making this country “great again.”
I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did.
Ever since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side.
The hard part will be maintaining it for the next seven weeks or so left in this race.
Republicans are spending over $100 million so far to turn voters against me and save their Senate majority – and this surge of dark money is taking a toll on our narrow polling lead.
We knew this was going to happen. We knew that far-right super PACs would swoop in with millions and that polls would tighten the closer we got to election day. We also know that we can fight back and win in North Carolina, but just as in elections past, I can’t do it alone.
[**_Please, Peter – with just hours left to hit our ambitious $2.5 million mid-month goal, will you chip in what you can to help me flip this seat, retake the Senate for Democrats and return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1338&amount=5&t=9&akid=3467%2E124072%2Eg0M1JA)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1338&amount=5&t=10&akid=3467%2E124072%2Eg0M1JA)

---
Thanks for being on this team.
Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1338&t=2&akid=3467%2E124072%2Eg0M1JA)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

Hi, Peter, I don't normally email you directly. That's usually Rick's job, not mine. But I'm the one who has to file our campaign finance report with the state tonight, and I wanted to make sure this reached you in time. I've watched Rick build this campaign without taking money from political bosses and party insiders. Tonight’s filing is the actual proof of that. It’s a public record of who's really funding this campaign. I want your name on it. Our campaign finance deadline hits tomorrow, Tuesday, September 15, at midnight. What lands in that filing tells the party bosses that the strength of our campaign is the people powering this race. You already know why I'm running: too many Maine families are doing everything right and still falling behind, while the people in power protect the system instead of the people. I'm not interested in managing that decline. I have a plan to cut the bottlenecks blocking housing, rein in utility profits, launch medical debt relief, and make sure every tax dollar actually works for Maine. And I'm going to fight for it. **But a people-powered campaign only works if the people show up for it.** And you have shown up, every time you've opened one of these. Now I'm asking you to be counted in the filing, too. Will you become an official supporter with a gift of $15, $35, or $60 before Tuesday's deadline? $15 puts you on the record as one of our grassroots supporters
$35 helps us reach roughly 1,400 voters by text
$60 puts our affordability message in front of about 2,400 Maine voters [**Add Your Name Before the Deadline →**](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=9_15_deadline_non_donor&n=3) We're $7,356 away from our goal for this filing. name: OnePA Team
subject: Make a plan to vote this November
body:
Check your registration, update your information, and make your plan to vote. | |
---
Peter, **Today is National Voter Registration Day, and there is one thing every eligible voter can do right now to protect our collective power this November: make sure you are registered and ready to vote.** Across the country, politicians are putting up new barriers to the ballot and pushing aggressive efforts to remove people from voter rolls. They want voting to be harder and more confusing. **We are not going to let those attacks convince us that our voices do not matter. Our votes are our power, and we are going to use them.** That starts with being prepared. Take a few minutes today to check your voter registration and make sure your name and address are correct. If you have moved, changed your name, or need to register for the first time, update your registration today. **Then make your plan. Decide how you are going to vote and when. If you plan to vote by mail, request your ballot as early as possible and return it early rather than waiting until the last minute.** [**Check your voter registration today and make sure you are ready to make your voice heard this November.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.nTQp_FEIcSHl649vCJCiciGHgA_sVZ7Psrn_WQ0V1FthiT-7PDCvgewQzc2JaBDgjT4Yb7lkc24ZE1R-aIzs2fYt2uOtH4Z4OSExL3AENRcdI1h1rfEm1xZSleKJzeurzrW_9Gj-ZpoMXJrl7z-urIEr8FpcAE-viXE3MRbXpyUutgSGHad9rS2KcW45iYCoU30zMQVcTCqK6t9FI7bTiQWKsmFgaVQeesMEIrM8qbZ0vYv75TjS7aFPS7q3YKPaq7N-aaErAH3i0w5KI0Ed0N5J6f2f6bKZ31-u-UXFUSYGujHJPYGwPmOYD0LZw9uEkFlf6DppQA0p1PPzZ0Tl4g/4u2/jMSCugYTTOSJ_S5rQSYnhA/h0/h001.MR31f25mzzFjgXwNITnIXQk_9EWHN9iVEFg60NfA_yA) | | [CHECK MY REGISTRATION](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.nTQp_FEIcSHl649vCJCiciGHgA_sVZ7Psrn_WQ0V1FthiT-7PDCvgewQzc2JaBDgwHZx8lS9ml8TK3aGuoRac5U_jRrYKSXRbbzwcvSdtzbRB-HtXj-A7JxjMYg2YW4X5uO-NKPLKU_uiGY5BugckWo50r6sKh3gC0rWbUCLYU4Idq-UUwpXfUz-Ed6gNPFSEbQAmidFh18H7oHzkJtAvqN33t0d5f5a-mYB4d9EahRWaFzN5r-LaXdIjcNWWgoIrVeXnRsEZ8gPj3qBXdHEAdojIk-t9jV6_wsFTqGRI8SzKrLlhn7HwyodhDzFbZvsBVL8vB7EyQ6Qcv1q6ykssA/4u2/jMSCugYTTOSJ_S5rQSYnhA/h1/h001.6BP-0JfN5vbmSB4MHDkPTCq2T4WvSnkbs0kb90fhZk8)
---
**Voting is only one part of building political power, but it is a part we cannot surrender.** Every election is an opportunity for our communities to decide who represents us, what gets funded, whose needs get heard, and who gets held accountable.
The people trying to make voting harder are counting on frustration and confusion to keep people home. Our answer is preparation, participation, and organizing our communities to show up.
So once you have checked your own registration, send this to somebody else. Ask your family, your friends, and your neighbors whether they are registered. Help someone update their address. Make sure the people around you know when and how they plan to vote.
[**Our democracy belongs to all of us. Let’s make sure we are registered, ready, and organized to use our power this November.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.nTQp_FEIcSHl649vCJCiciGHgA_sVZ7Psrn_WQ0V1FthiT-7PDCvgewQzc2JaBDgGJ24ouQ444-yvwi4kRRBUBqQ5sgNeddHjENH_DqjDb51WNoVJj3n8jRgq0dHwm0bEFIe8lT-pKM8zq3WnKbTGY0Nu2OB_zaKPgG5W6s-XLjfdvWfVOnQZ9q0r2X-EH_mjbZ8E7ZnU_J3YMWGWFzfWfWU_98CqGWzixTMpzKbrGDl_JXzU1KQcV63xhQo-vpNDRNrRq4hKf_4vnhlvb1uJpUhWF-PjsjOUkQ84QPgETqmu0RI1e3GCYtH14zdKacr9dZZPllFdRHu2ugeD6zTTA/4u2/jMSCugYTTOSJ_S5rQSYnhA/h2/h001.899EmLO7hGVKtD26iepnktNHuLpmJ-Lp879TRXufCTY)
Together we will build power.

**Will my mail-in ballot be counted?****** At this point, you may have whiplash amid the rapidly changing litigation over the Trump administration’s proposed mail-voting restrictions. As of mid-September, Pennsylvania officials affirm that eligible voters can still vote by mail for the November 3, 2026, General Election.
Pennsylvania voters can take practical steps to make sure their mail ballot is counted: apply on time, follow every instruction, sign and date the return envelope where required, and return the ballot early enough for the county election office to receive it by 8:00pm on Election Day.
**Registered PA-11 voters who choose to vote by mail have several return options:**
1\. Return your completed mail ballot in the mail in self-addressed return envelope to:
**Lancaster:** Lancaster County Voter Registration and Board of ElectionsP.O. Box 2139 Lancaster, PA 17608
**York:** York County Elections & Voter Registration2401 Pleasant Valley Road, Suite 219, York, PA 17402

2\. Deliver your own mail ballot to your county elections office or a county-designated drop-off location:
**Lancaster:** 150 North Queen Street, Suite 117, Lancaster, PA 17603
**York:****Downtown** , 28 East Market Street, B003, York, PA 17401**East York** , 2401 Pleasant Valley Road, Suite 219, York, PA 17402

If you are voting by mail, carefully follow all instructions included with your ballot. Place the ballot in the secrecy envelope, then place that envelope in the return envelope. Complete, sign, and date the return envelope where indicated.
**If you receive a mail-in ballot and choose to vote in person:**
If you receive a mail-in ballot but decide to vote in person on Nov. 3, bring your mail ballot, secrecy envelope, and return envelope to your polling place so they can be surrendered. After surrendering those materials, you can vote by regular ballot. If you do not have all required materials, you may vote by provisional ballot.
**You can check the status of your mail-in ballot at the[PA Dept of State Website](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgCq8X470CC8q2cMhfd/MSNczvF9m9wy).**

**Deadlines for the November 3, 2026, General Election**

* **October 19** : Last day to register to vote or update your voter registration for the General Election.
* Register to Vote [here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsGQ0v2YvQCvMSCfQRLRNh/CGQP2EqzURuz).
* Update or change your Registration [here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsGsLdEzJmIqWiGUoGKB5l/N7voxY2wBCmF).
* Check your registration status [here](https://matj3.r.a.d.sendibm1.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsHKgLRPi8OlgyKKC5Iunp/DJvB0xTP8tAB).

* **5:00pm on October 27** : Your application for a mail-in or absentee ballot must be received by your county election office.

* **8:00pm on November 3** : Your county election office must receive your completed mail ballot by this time. A postmark by 8:00pm is not enough.

**Voting Information Quick Links:**

## **Week in Review**
---
**Manheim Township September 11th Remembrance Ceremony** The solemn event included the placing of wreaths and retiring the flag that flew over the Township memorial. Those gathered reflected on the unity our country experienced in the days following, and how we should hold to those ideals today. Nancy recalled, “It's been 25 years, and every moment of that day is etched in my memory forever. May we always honor those who perished, and those who answered the call to help.”
**Door Knocking Around Lancaster** MusicFest brought shaded skies and pleasant temperatures to Buchanan Park on Saturday, September 12. The event was a great chance to support local musicians, craftspeople, and food vendors and to talk with community members.
The Mannion campaign team spent the afternoon in the park as well as canvassing the neighborhood for Nancy and other local candidates – spreading the message that voters have a choice in November!

---
---
**Lancaster County Democratic Committee End-of-Summer Picnic** The annual Lancaster County Democratic Committee end-of-summer picnic was held in Long's Park on Sunday, September 13. Approximately two hundred people came out to share delicious BBQ and be inspired by the slate of candidates. Thanks to everyone who helped organize the event!.

Friends,
I'll get straight to it: my opponent, Shaun Finnie, just spent nearly **$1 million** on a TV ad blitz.
A million dollars. In one shot.
That's the kind of money Finnie is willing to throw around to try to buy this seat – and it tells you everything about how seriously he's taking this race. He knows conservatives here are fired up. And he knows the only way he wins is by trying to outspend us.
I didn't get into this race to be outworked by someone who thinks a bigger checkbook beats a bold vision. I got in this race to fight for limited government, secure borders, and the conservative values that will make life more affordable and the American Dream more attainable, and no ad buy changes that.
**But I won't pretend that a $1 million spend doesn't matter. It does. And right now, it's go time.**
We don't need to match Finnie dollar for dollar. We need grassroots support – real conservatives like you stepping up so we can get our message on the air, in mailboxes, and in front of every voter in this district before Election Day.

On August 5, 2026, Senior U.S. District Judge William B. Shubb of the Eastern District of California granted a preliminary injunction in Kory v. Bonta, prohibiting California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the state's medical licensing boards from investigating, prosecuting, or sanctioning Drs. Pierre Kory, Le Trinh Hoang, and Brian Tyson based on the viewpoint of COVID-19 medical advice they provide to patients.
The case stems from California's AB 2098, enacted in 2022, which authorized the Medical Board of California to discipline physicians for COVID-19 "misinformation" that contradicted the "scientific consensus." Though the legislature later repealed AB 2098, the plaintiffs argued the boards retained policies that still chilled physician-patient speech. Judge Shubb applied two recent U.S. Supreme Court decisions in granting the injunction, signaling that viewpoint-based regulation of professional speech faces heightened scrutiny. Dr. Kory, a pulmonary and critical care physician known for advocating ivermectin and other treatments at odds with federal guidance, framed the ruling as preventing the government from "telling doctors what they can say."
**Republican Governors Side with Democrats to Block Immigration Enforcement**
A report from Blaze Media highlights that Republican Governor Spencer Cox of Utah and Kevin Stitt of Oklahoma, also a Republican, have aligned with Democrats to expand migrant work visa programs, which the article characterizes as conspiring to "import more migrants" and undermine Trump's immigration reform agenda...

# **[The AI"Extinction Circus" is in town and everybody has a role to play](https://substack.com/redirect/d2ece8a1-aaf4-48f2-96f6-02316d156222?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Democrats led by Bernie Sanders want the government to halt AI, agents, data centers, the whole stack, and Larry Kudlow's branding it an election-year ruse, same playbook as the climate hoax. David Sacks already called it regulatory capture or a psy-op. China isn't slowing down one inch, why would they, they're laughing all the way to the bank! Everybody in the AI extinction circus is talking their own book while the 10-year sat above 5% Monday and Tuesday and crude kept climbing. Overnight index swaps have 24.9 basis points locked for Wednesday's FOMC. Amodei, Musk, and Altman want a pause. Zuckerberg wants speed. Huang told Trump they will not let it happen.
* **Winners?** Nvidia and Trump, treating chips as national-security steel, plus Meta, which already owns distribution and profits if inference gets cheaper without a new regulatory moat, every chip-and-power operator still pouring concrete. America keeps the throttle open. Capital follows the buildout, not the sermon from the safety choir.
* **Losers?** Amodei, Altman, every safety CEO begging Washington for a pause that looks like a margin moat, Sanders, Democrats, Anthropic, OpenAI, the METR shop Sacks just framed as a cartel in altruist clothing, plus equity desks that sold Monday while oil stayed bid. Their regulatory-moat pitch just got priced as midterm politics.
* **Next?** Wednesday's hike prints, oil stays tight off the Saudi pipeline and Hormuz snarl, and the pause lobby keeps preaching while Rabobank keeps calling it a book. Election season turns this into a binary. Either the pause lobby wins a leash, or Trump keeps calling it a hoax and the data-center boom runs.

This is the same regulatory-moat play I called in **["Anthropic begged for AI rules then Trump sent them to the guillotine."](https://substack.com/redirect/d7a441e0-90fb-4e22-b241-50f5ee3e10c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
They asked for the whip. Trump and Huang just told them no. Load the chip and energy complex. Short the sermon. This town still eats its own when you beg for chains.

* **Winners?** Hyperscalers and private-market control freaks who keep OpenAI off a public clock while they lock compute, power, and the narrative without quarterly interrogations.

* **Next?** No listing this year. Independent evaluators get "employee-like access." The safety sermon buys time. The S-1 sits in a drawer until the politics cool.

# [Five-percent Treasuries finally pay you to sit still](https://substack.com/redirect/d2ece8a1-aaf4-48f2-96f6-02316d156222?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The 10-year just smashed 5%, the highest print since 2007, and the tourists are screaming. Cullen Roche calls this escape velocity: at these coupons, five-year-and-under duration can eat another 1% yield spike and still show black ink. The Fed Survey wants at least two hikes this year. Oil and Iran are the accelerant.
* **Winners?** Buyers of five-year-and-under Treasuries locking $50,000 a year on every $1 million at 5%. Income finally pays you to sit still while the long end bleeds.
* **Losers?** Long-duration tourists who treated bonds like a savings account, and anyone still waiting for 2020 coupons. Another 1% up the curve still knocks the 10-year around.
* **Next?** Wednesday's 25-basis-point hike is the near-money. Then the market prices whether two hikes this year stick while crude keeps the inflation tape hot.

This is not a hero long. It's arithmetic. Roche's cushion shows up inside five years, not out at the 10-year where you just printed a 2007 high. Clip the coupon, keep duration short, and let the deficit-and-oil crowd keep lighting the long end on fire. Yield is a feature again. Duration is the bill.

# [This startup more than triples to $5 billion and coding agents just got a real price tag](https://substack.com/redirect/d2ece8a1-aaf4-48f2-96f6-02316d156222?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Factory just more than tripled. The AI coding shop that builds autonomous agents printed a $5 billion valuation on a $200 million check from Khosla Ventures, Blackstone, and Sequoia, with Marc Benioff and Brad Gerstner riding shotgun as angels. Five months ago this thing was marked at $1.5 billion. That's not a step-up. That's a stampede.
* **Winners?** Khosla, Blackstone, Sequoia, Benioff, Gerstner, and CEO Matan Grinberg, who just sold Wall Street a $5 billion ticket on coding agents.
* **Losers?** Late-stage tourists who missed the $1.5 billion print, plus every human coding bench now competing with agents priced like a public software company.
* **Next?** Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX already ship coding tools. Factory just made the private-market price of that war $5 billion. More marks follow.

This is hot money chasing the one AI product companies actually use. Autonomous agents that code, marked at $5 billion five months after a $1.5 billion round. The labs can preach extinction. The check writers just paid up for the shovel that writes the code. Load the picks. Let the sermon starve.

clean_body: Friends, This is going to make you angry. New Yorkers pay more for electricity than almost anyone in the country, and we get less for it. | Friends, This is going to make you angry. New Yorkers pay more for electricity than almost anyone in the country, and we get less for it. Look at the numbers. New York residential electricity runs about 29.49 cents per kWh. The U.S. average is 18.34 cents. Texas is 15.94. Florida is 15.10. | | Here is the part that should make you furious. Buried inside your utility bill is a hidden property tax. It is 14.3 percent of your total, folded into the delivery charge and never shown as its own line. You are being taxed and you cannot even see it. As Comptroller, I will drag these hidden charges into the light and demand answers for every dollar New Yorkers are forced to pay. To do that, I need your help right now. | New Yorkers deserve a Comptroller who protects their retirement, their tax dollars, and their future. | | | | | Thank you, Joseph Hernandez Republican for NYS Comptroller | | Hernandez for New York, 697 3rd Avenue, #106, New York, NY 10017

Troy Jackson defended his purchase of an Augusta house and more than $160,000 in legislative payments at a Sunday, Sept. 13, forum in Biddeford, citing Ethics Commission decisions that did not resolve questions about his mortgage or travel claims.
"It just happened that I had the house and that's where I stayed," Jackson said at the event, where he unsuccessfully attempted to exclude Maine Wire reporters.
"The [Augusta] house was just a much easier place for me to keep my stuff," he said, comparing it with keeping belongings in his car when hotel accommodations were unavailable.
As the Maine Wire reported in August 2023, Jackson and Lana Pelletier bought the property in September 2019 with an FHA-insured mortgage. The agreement required occupancy within 60 days and use as a principal residence for at least one year, subject to specified exceptions. Jackson signed the agreement and initialed the occupancy provision.

---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c3e3e4ec-0101-43a7-9dd8-f52dbbb3f068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jackson has consistently said that he never made the Augusta house his primary residence, insisting that he's always been a resident of Allagash.
"This is unfortunate, but I never really read the forms," Jackson told the newspaper in September 2023.
"I was going off his interpretation," Jackson said, laying blame at the feet of his mortgage broker.
The mortgage broker, Michael G. Wilson, disputed Jackson's account, telling the Maine Wire that his firm followed FHA guidelines and expected borrowers to read and complete their applications.
According to the Federal Housing Administration, "mortgage fraud is characterized by a material misstatement, misrepresentation, or omission in relation to a mortgage loan, which is then relied upon by a lender."
"Mortgage fraud is a criminal offense investigated and prosecuted by law enforcement," the FHA website states. "Civil and criminal penalties for mortgage fraud at the state and federal level can be severe and may include convictions and prison time, restitution payments, state fines, and/or probation."
At the Biddeford forum, Jackson cited unanimous Ethics Commission votes in defense of the FHA loan he obtained by claiming he would become a resident of Augusta.
In October 2023, the commission voted 5-0 to take no further action on a complaint questioning the Allagash address he supplied in campaign filings.
That decision did not establish whether Jackson satisfied his mortgage agreement or made the trips underlying his travel claims. Commissioners distinguished legal residency from mortgage occupancy requirements.
The Ethics Commission's October 2023 meeting minutes explicitly record that the commission did not oversee legislative reimbursements and that alleged mortgage misstatements belonged before other authorities.
Jackson also described the purchase as a costly mistake -- which is an odd way to describe an investment that earned him more than $80,000 after taxes.
"I just got elected as Senate President. I knew I was going to be spending a lot more time down there," he said. "That was the biggest mistake in my life. Not because of what this is, but because of the house. It's a real money pit."
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=215744353&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE1NzQ0MzUzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODk1MDMxMzMsImV4cCI6MTc5MjA5NTEzMywiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.2q8tM8rKJsbx3ozpLzvxxhXuP8tBrzHp863Pgcm6OrE)
In fact, Jackson's original purchase amount for the home was $220,000, but he sold it in 2021 for $323,000. Jackson has said he paid roughly $20,000 in capital gains taxes, which means he earned $87,000 flipping a home he acquired with an FHA loan.
Jackson's Augusta crash pad is relevant not just because of the constitutional requirement that Maine lawmakers live in their districts or the apparent mortgage fraud Jackson has admitted to, but also because he holds the record for the most mileage reimbursement dollars ever received by a Maine state lawmaker.
According to records obtained by the Maine Wire through a Freedom of Access Act (FOAA) request, Jackson received more than [$160k](https://substack.com/redirect/50fc5b5d-081f-423e-8c2a-dc3c6abed009?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in legislative reimbursements from 2019 to 2023 -- money for which Jackson would not have to pay taxes.
Remarkably, Jackson accumulated these reimbursements despite having the house in Augusta, just miles from the State House.
At the forum on Sunday, Jackson alleged that the sale of his Augusta house means that he couldn't have improperly reimbursed himself for untravelled miles.
"But I fixed it up and sold it to a person two years later," Jackson said Sunday. "So the whole argument about the four years and all that falls on that."
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..qvfpz5zCuFXtrXSE9dOPh4R12FkerS7QXRYKKsf6EjU?)
After selling the house, however, Jackson rented another residence in Augusta, a fact he acknowledged in 2023.
The Maine Wire published photographs showing vehicles associated with Jackson at the property throughout the 2023-2024 legislative session.
Maine Revenue Services subsequently listed the condo as Jackson's "last known address" in a 2025 lien for unpaid income taxes.

It’s $1 from your friend, your neighbor, and thousands of folks you don’t know but who share your commitment to this fight. That’s what it’ll take to win. So with our mid-month deadline just hours away, we need you to chip in $1 – or more if you can spare it – to help us reach our $1.75 million goal and keep building the momentum it’ll take to flip this seat in less than 50 days. = | | = Thank you, Team Sherrod | | Note: This email only reflects donations made online with this email address. If you've made a previous contribution via check or with a different email address/phone number, you may not see it here – but know that Sherrod and our entire team are deeply grateful for your support. = Hey there! It's Sherrod Brown. There's nobody fighting for Ohioans in the U.S. Senate right now, and I won't sit on the sidelines while working people get screwed over by large corporations and wealthy political donors. If you work hard, you should be able to afford a decent life. But the reality is, life is too expensive. Costs are going up. Wages are staying stagnant. Working people are working harder than ever before, and they're not getting their share of the profit. This campaign is all about changing that – and election analysts say we have a strong shot at winning in November. But I'll need your help to pull it off: My opponent is a Washington insider being propped up by the Republican establishment, and he's got virtually unlimited resources. That's not how our campaign works. We're a grassroots movement, and that means we rely on ordinary people chipping in a couple bucks. = If you'd like to receive exclusive updates from my team, you can text "OHIO" to 64054. name: State Representative Ryan Chamberlin
subject: 9/11, In District, and Marion County Florida
body:
Newsletter from Rep. Ryan Chamberlin

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/repryanchamberlin/newsletter-from-rep-ryan-chamberlin-kqs1grv7ud-12935701?e=d1c1b9864f)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
### NEWSLETTER FROM REP. RYAN CHAMBERLIN
---
| | Friends and Neighbors,

**Thank you again for reelecting me as your Representative.** Since the election, I have been moving nonstop, and I want to share with you some of the things I have done.
As always, please do not hesitate to [**contact my office**](https://us.list-manage.com/QTa1ryeVvPy?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=3wcABTnakq-jQUsGEpkRekSJCu2JXkILb6QkFmka9RUnlSJjSYqsjKxkSFc=) if there is something we can do for you. My team and I would be more than happy to help you in any way we can.

---
| |
### Remembering 9/11
---
|
---
| | 25 years later, we stand together as Americans, remembering the lives and families forever changed that day.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| | Friday was a special day... The Morning Started out in Ocala at the 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony. I then was honored to speak with our first responders at the Belleview Freedom Walk as we gathered to remember and honor the lives lost.
---
| |
### In the District
---
|
---
| | Joined **Marion Senior Services in Welcoming Lt. Gov. Collins to Ocala.** Marion Senior services spoke to him about their Senior Crisis Mobile Response Team. Then the Lt. Gov. spoke about his Operation Senior Shield.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Met with the team at **Heart of Florida Health Center** to learn more about the vital work they do throughout Marion County.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Stopped by the **Boys & Girls Clubs’ annual luncheon** to hear an update on the incredible work they’ve continued to do across Marion County.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | Had a great conversation over coffee with Realtors® about **the importance of eliminating property taxes in Florida.**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | Attended the**United Way of Marion County’s 65th Anniversary Annual Luncheon** and helped celebrate **65 years of serving our community.** And a huge congrats to our **County Clerk, Greg Harrell,** for receiving the **Bonnie Heath Legacy Award.**
---
|
---
|
---
| | Honored to have joined **Attorney General James Uthmeier** for an important press conference on the investigation into **Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs)** and efforts to **lower prescription drug costs.**
---
|
---
|
---
| | Great to meet with **Isaiah House 117-Marion County** for the first time and learn about the incredible work they’re doing to support children in foster care. For more information, check out their website.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Enjoyed meeting with **Ellie Trueman, Bonnie Heath, and Katie Glynn of the Ocala Horse Alliance Foundation** to learn more about **The Black Stallion Reading Project** and how successful it has been for the past 7 years.
---
|
---
|
---
| | I appreciated meeting **Pastor De Jesus** to learn about **God Belongs in My City** and its **IronPath initiative.**
---
|
---
|
---
| | Stopped by **Zero Suicide Marion** and had the pleasure of speaking and learning more about the critical work they’re doing across our community to prevent suicide and save lives.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | Had the opportunity to meet up with **Florida’s next Lieutenant Governor, Bryan Avila,** to discuss the future of Marion County and how we can continue supporting the Horse Capital of the World.
---
|
---
|
---
| | Enjoyed attending the **ROCKS Annual Fundraising event** and helping them celebrate 10 years!
---
|
---
| | Thank you for your feedback and for being interested in our state government. These are important issues affecting everyone, and I need **your** help to make progress for our constituents. I look forward to sharing with you again soon.
Best regards,
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | **Ryan Chamberlin****State Representative****District 24**
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | | | [](https://us.list-manage.com/Zy4Muzv09bf?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=-QastcPdyZM14ez_ugrajhNMmiFNUPdFcBwH_qkZKqkltydnjrHmFm7W7xg=)
---
[](https://us.list-manage.com/cB2T7p4cfcW?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=20wMH3KwXUQvOZMKa8ia53rsq9OKfikYQXw416ergzdTkH9pb90L-1Li3TI=)
---

body:
This story is at the heart of my Administration

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139266868/646790848/-2120664357?refcode=email_091526_story&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YzBhNjUzNi00M2IxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YmgufER8pUCnM4IcMDmvdmk5cUOWtUG3CO7Tn9EIGZA=) I want to tell you a story that represents the heart of my Administration. I’ll admit: It’s a bit on the longer side, and I hope you’ll read the whole thing. [_**But if you’re in a hurry, I could really use your support in these final days before mail-in ballots go out. Can you chip in just a few bucks to help us reach thousands of undecided voters while we still have the chance?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139266869/646790876/-2120664357?refcode=email_091526_story&amounts=5,25,50,100,250,500,1000&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YzBhNjUzNi00M2IxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=YmgufER8pUCnM4IcMDmvdmk5cUOWtUG3CO7Tn9EIGZA=) Derek, I remember what the experts told me after a section of I-95 collapsed in Philly just months after I took office. They told me it would take months to reopen the roadway. Months of gridlock. Months of traffic jams. Months of headaches for working Pennsylvanians. The next day, I issued a proclamation of disaster emergency to cut through the red tape and provide Commonwealth agencies with the resources they needed to do their jobs. Hours later, crews started working around the clock. Four days after the collapse? We set up a 24/7 livestream of the construction site, so Pennsylvanians could see exactly what their government was up to. No vague, ambiguous statements. No promises without evidence to back it up. The following day? Pennsylvania union workers began to lay the foundation for the interim roadway. Not long after, we made it official: **We reopened six lanes of traffic on I-95 just twelve days after an unprecedented collapse.** We didn’t accept the status quo. We buckled down and got to work. And Derek, I’ve brought that same mindset to everything I do as your Governor. When I took office, political pundits all across the country believed we wouldn’t get anything done. I was one of the only Governors in the nation working with a divided legislature — a Republican-controlled State Senate, and a Democratic-controlled State House. In many other states, it was a recipe for gridlock and disaster. But here in Pennsylvania? **We got sh*t done.** Record funding for our public schools. Free breakfasts for every Pennsylvania K-12 student. Ten tax cuts for families, seniors, and small businesses across our Commonwealth. I still hear it from the pundits all the time, Derek: Delivering real, lasting progress in a swing state is impossible — a thing of the past. **But we’re proving them wrong every damn day.** [_**If that’s the kind of leadership that speaks to you, I’m counting on your support right now. I’ll admit: It’s a bit on the longer side, and I hope you’ll read the whole thing. = Derek, I remember what the experts told me after a section of I-95 collapsed in Philly just months after I took office. They told me it would take months to reopen the roadway. Months of gridlock. Months of traffic jams. Months of headaches for working Pennsylvanians. The next day, I issued a proclamation of disaster emergency to cut through the red tape and provide Commonwealth agencies with the resources they needed to do their jobs. Hours later, crews started working around the clock. Four days after the collapse? We set up a 24/7 livestream of the construction site, so Pennsylvanians could see exactly what their government was up to. No vague, ambiguous statements. No promises without evidence to back it up. The following day? Pennsylvania union workers began to lay the foundation for the interim roadway. Not long after, we made it official: We reopened six lanes of traffic on I-95 just twelve days after an unprecedented collapse. We didn’t accept the status quo. We buckled down and got to work. And Derek, I’ve brought that same mindset to everything I do as your Governor. When I took office, political pundits all across the country believed we wouldn’t get anything done. # [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260915-1&t=1&akid=4016%2E587540%2E-SEK4a)
Peter, today is an important day.
**But before we discuss the importance of today, I want you to go double check your voter registration status[here.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/5816?t=2&akid=4016%2E587540%2E-SEK4a)**
September 15th is National Voter Registration Day.
Today marks a coordinated effort from organizations across the country to register eligible voters, ensuring that everyone is prepared to cast their ballots in November.
According to data from the 2020 U.S. Census, as many as 1 in 4 eligible Americans are **not** registered to vote. Every election, millions of Americans are unable to cast their ballot because of a missed deadline, an outdated registration, or because they don’t know how to register. **Now I want you to take a moment and think about your friends, family, kids, or coworkers. Is there anyone who could use a reminder from you to register to vote today?**
Young voters historically have lower registration levels than any other age group, despite making up a growing number of the population. In order to see the change we want to see this November, we have to make sure everyone is prepared to cast their votes. **Text your kids, nieces, and nephews today and remind them to check where they’re registered, what their polling place is, and whether they’re planning to vote in person or by mail!**
Because of the growing number of young voters, it is even more important that we fight for the representation we deserve. Millennials and Gen Z make up over 40% of the United States population, while the median age of Senators is 64 and the median age in the House is 57.
**A lot is on the line this November, and it is more important than ever that you exercise your democratic right to vote.**
Your vote is your most powerful tool in exercising and celebrating democracy. Now that we’ve made sure your voter registration is up to date, send this to a friend to make sure theirs is too.
**[Will you pitch in $5 now to make sure our candidates have the resources to get out the vote and win in November?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_1_voter.zv54xi&refcode=em20260915-4016&amount=5&t=3&akid=4016%2E587540%2E-SEK4a)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_1_voter.zv54xi&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4016&t=22&akid=4016%2E587540%2E-SEK4a)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

clean_body: | | | Peter, With the midterm elections only 7 weeks away, it’s time to lock in. This is our chance to take back the House and Senate, to put a stop to Trump’s disastrous war in Iran, to lower the sky-high cost of living, and to pass legislation to rein in Big Tech. The Supreme Court’s disgraceful Louisiana v. Callais decision sparked attacks on voting rights across the country, and especially in the South. But we refuse to give in and pull out of the region. Now more than ever, we need to invest in working class southerners who are hungry for change and ready to fight for it by electing leaders like Angie Nixon and Justin J. Pearson. Angie Nixon is a WFP member, labor organizer, community advocate, small-business owner, state lawmaker, and mother who has spent years leading a coalition to promote voting rights. Last month, she defied the odds and a political establishment who thought she had no shot by winning her Florida primary for U.S. Senate despite being outraised by her opponent 16-to-1. Justin J. Pearson is a public servant, community organizer, and proud fighter. When Republicans expelled him from the Tennessee House of Representatives for protesting gun violence, he refused to back down and was reinstated to his seat a week later to continue the fight. Now, he’s running for Congress in the face of racist redistricting to build a government that works for all of us. In solidarity, Team WFP Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. I first met musician Morgxn in the Capitol rotunda, hearing him sing right after the 2023 “Tennessee Three” expulsions

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/56e08b801268/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363863?e=dc5f639d62)

| | Hey friends,
I'm thrilled to have my friends Morgxn & Gabriel join me this week on the pod!

[**[Click Here to LISTEN NOW]**](https://us.list-manage.com/15Yjl3L0QLG?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
I first met musician Morgxn in the Capitol rotunda, hearing him sing during the 2023 “Tennessee Three” expulsions, and I've loved getting to know him and his husband Gabriel ever since. This week I sat down with both of them to talk about [Fruity Farm](https://us.list-manage.com/eyYmjMIY3P5?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), the agroforestry farm they've built in Sumner County that's become an unexpected hub of community and resistance, especially now that it hosts[ Affirming Sumner](https://us.list-manage.com/SSyn1ymkHuA?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), the county's only Pride celebration, after other venues backed out under pressure.
We get into a wild biology lesson about pawpaws (no, not your grandpa), a pretty remarkable story about confronting a state legislator over anti-LGBTQ legislation, and what it looks like to build a life of love and resilience in a place that doesn't always make that easy.

[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/rtw6k9CvlKV?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

**Check out**[**Affirming Sumner**](https://us.list-manage.com/fYnHqCFyWAQ?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**on September 19th!**[**[Click Here to RSVP- I’ll be there at 1:00 so see you there!]**](https://us.list-manage.com/ClKgLQ8Yb4L?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)

**Listen to Morgxn’s album**[** Heartland**](https://us.list-manage.com/EAuzxG7jT5A?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**, out now!**
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

_Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. _ A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance.

They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. **Their hearts were still with the children. **Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, **they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes**. The child who once needed someone to find her**grew up to help care for children who need to be found. **That is**restoration**. That is **hope**. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects **between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day**.

clean_body: They found Nadia at a Metro station A frightened 15-year-old was given a chance. See where she is today. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance. They told her something every child deserves to hear: You are loved. They promised to protect her and help her get an education. And Nadia willingly went with them. She left behind a horrible life and came home to parents who would raise her as their own. Friend, Nadia's story is one reason Sound of Freedom Foundation works with groups like House Parent Project.My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie Sound of Freedom because after learning what traffickers do to innocent children, I could not simply look away.For me, it stopped being a movie. It became a calling. Today, the Sound of Freedom Foundation carries that mission forward. Our mission is simple: Stop the sale of God 's children. House Parent Project shares that commitment. Their house parents give these children the love and care they've never known. And Nadia shows what can happen when a child is not abandoned. A couple of years after her rescue, the team found Nadia's sister, Sofia. She was suffering through many of the same horrors. They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. Their hearts were still with the children. Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes. The child who once needed someone to find hergrew up to help care for children who need to be found. That isrestoration. That is hope. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day. When it is safe, they work to restore children to healthy homes with family members. When that cannot happen, the homes may raise these children as their own until they grow up, get jobs, and go to college. More than 40 children that were residents stayed to become staff after they grew up. Others have grown up and married national pastors and missionaries. But there's a problem. The phone never stops ringing. There is always another child. Another crisis and another need. And the resources are slim. Providing three meals for one child costs about $4 a day. And that doesn't include clothes, shoes, diapers, or all the other things children need. Jesus said: " Let the little children come to me." (Matthew 19:14) I believe we have a duty to hear the cries of children who cannot protect themselves. Because when good people stay quiet, evil has room to grow. But when good people stand together,lives can change. Nadia is living proof. Friend, will you help us stand with House Parent Project and the house parents caring for children like Nadia today? "=" $25 can help feed a child fornearly a week $50 can help feed a child fornearly two weeks $100 can help feed a childfor25 days $200 can help**feedtwo children for 25 days That 's three meals every day. Maybe we cannot answer every call today. But together, we can help answer the next one. Please give now. And please pray for the children and for those caring for them. Share this mission with someone you love. Because this truth must be heard around the world: God 's children are not for sale. With gratitude and prayer, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. It costs about $4 to provide one child with three meals for one day**. Friends,

There are less than 50 days between now and the November 2026 election.

**_[Today, on National Voter Registration Day, I hope you'll take a moment to double-check your voter registration.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139269536/646799816/-667246286?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84ODM1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzMzNjMjQ5Ny00YWIxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hG1VKH2RfHytF_F4MiKC402Sx4RDQQgPSFgHFA061xw=&emci=76db5eb6-45b1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=333c2497-4ab1-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=36327723)_**

When we moved to California, my mother ran a polling place out of our living room. Today, I have the privilege of administering elections in the largest state in the union.

Friends,

Today marks the beginning of Hispanic Heritage Month, a celebration of the vibrant and diverse Latino communities here in the Hudson Valley and across the country. This weekend, I had the privilege of joining the Haverstraw 15th Annual United Latin Festival and the Ossining Hispanic Festival in Nelson Park — two incredible celebrations of history, music, food, and culture.

We were also joined by the Hispanic Democrats of Westchester to knock on doors and speak directly with Latino voters about what matters most to them in this election.

Last week, I had the chance to stop by some amazing Latino-owned restaurants and small businesses in Sleepy Hollow, including Sabrosura Peruana, Justin’s Deli & Cafe, La Esquina Del Sabor Latino, and Los Andes Bakery. We had important conversations about the impact of Donald Trump’s reckless tariffs — which Mike Lawler has voted for eight times — on their ability to run successful small businesses and support their families. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMctRoxlFO9O82fTB5zU1O8H2T10xcmixfoRUcqRkRyN8qhON8I23ASf5CXzxfRr4938LpoK69vH-eSQHHT-uwlBrHzzirCBDifpXaO2tXvxASxWyO7LIsUMicqihUDNT2EasyADdIUXtWka2VsdusRwyEePs22KnJq4_JoUeUOavykyuvMcVOIlWjVRSQNExMxfXYOHz4Z1YU7KYqysg-Srr9ENuuC4tOeETeUYOmDdat26Qg__juP1j4hR8T9EYnzfKWsyLpXhg6WwwUd8J-gC4hI9z2T8KCCdelo2idTP818gBfZ5O1WQbD3dOB9xUUyiVru1dqCYBFbSssjpzSVs/4u2/0EEtNAKKTxmi4AUXImDdpw/h0/h001.K5u1mzOZmR5T4SAiSPH6MyPtt-yoj17SxdrEVtfB1Qw)
The Hudson Valley is home to rich and vibrant Hispanic communities that contribute so much to our country. But right now, many of our neighbors are living in fear because this administration has turned immigration enforcement into a weapon instead of a tool to go after violent criminals and keep our families safe.
As a former military police officer, I know how important it is to ensure our immigration enforcement is focused on violent criminals, not grandmas and nurses.
With gratitude and fire, Cait Conley

This weekend, I had the privilege of joining the Haverstraw 15th Annual United Latin Festival and the Ossining Hispanic Festival in Nelson Park — two incredible celebrations of history, music, food, and culture. We were also joined by the Hispanic Democrats of Westchester to knock on doors and speak directly with Latino voters about what matters most to them in this election. Last week, I had the chance to stop by some amazing Latino-owned restaurants and small businesses in Sleepy Hollow, including Sabrosura Peruana, Justin’s Deli & Cafe, La Esquina Del Sabor Latino, and Los Andes Bakery. We had important conversations about the impact of Donald Trump’s reckless tariffs — which Mike Lawler has voted for eight times — on their ability to run successful small businesses and support their families. The Hudson Valley is home to rich and vibrant Hispanic communities that contribute so much to our country. But right now, many of our neighbors are living in fear because this administration has turned immigration enforcement into a weapon instead of a tool to go after violent criminals and keep our families safe. As a former military police officer, I know how important it is to ensure our immigration enforcement is focused on violent criminals, not grandmas and nurses. **This isn 't about Democrats vs. Republicans. It's about who's fighting for us vs. who's fighting for themselves and the ultra-rich and powerful.**

If Dan wants to run against a socialist, he should move back home to New York. Because that's not who I am.
I'm focused on the things that actually matter to people. Lowering costs. Fighting corruption and fraud. Bringing people together to solve local problems.
**Our message is resonating with people, but we need to make sure we don 't get drowned out by Dan's BS. So I need your help.**

**Trump says he’ll pay every adult U.S. citizen _$5,000_ if Republicans win the midterms. ** Not only is this BS, but it’s an insult. name: Gina for Texas
subject: Gina is already making history, Peter
body:
Gina’s candidacy comes with so many firsts for the great state of Texas.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Gina’s candidacy comes with so many firsts for the great state of Texas.
**She is the _first_ person to tie in polls with Greg Abbott and is the closest anyone has come to ending his 12 year reign.**
Gina is already making history, being the closest anyone has come to flipping the Texas governorship in over 30 years. No Democrat has won a statewide race since 1994, and **Gina would be the _first_ Democratic governor elected since 1991.**
**Gina would also be the _first_ governor from the Rio Grande Valley.** She was born in McAllen and grew up in Brownsville, two border cities in the southernmost part of Texas. Texas has never had a governor raised on the border, and her upbringing rooted in Valley culture, hard work, and determination are what have helped her in her political career.

| | | Folks, it’s a triple-seven day.

We are exactly **seven** weeks out from Election Day, and I’m here to give you **seven** good reasons to chip in **seven** bucks (or $70!) to my campaign for Congress. Let’s get into it:
1. I have proven over decades that**I will show up, work the double shift, and face down the special interests to deliver for my community.** The families of Virginia’s Fighting Fifth are my people, and every single person in this beautiful district deserves a champion in their corner.

2. The midterms are our chance to **put our country back on the path to sanity** after Trump and his cronies have dragged us into dark depths of corruption that have shoved the American dream further and further from reach for so many people.

3. Our government runs on checks and balances, and this GOP-led Congress we’re stuck with right now isn’t holding up their end of the bargain. They’ve sold out the American people to please their President and protect their power, and they haven’t looked back once. We need to take back the House to**restore a Constitutional check on the Trump White House!**

4. The path to a Democratic majority in the House runs squarely through VA-05. **If we flip this seat blue, we can flip the entire House blue** – and deliver a courageous majority that will govern instead of grovel.

5. My opponent **John McGuire is a literal January 6er.** And as if that wasn’t disqualifying enough, he’s continued to betray his fellow Americans with each vote against his constituents’ best interests, from the Big Ugly Bill that shuttered rural health clinics and gutted Medicaid, to continuing this dangerous and pointless war in Iran, to enabling Trump’s tariffs that are bankrupting farmers and businesses across VA.

6. We’re building **a common-sense coalition** of all kinds of people all across this district – Democrats, Republicans, and Independents alike – who are sick and tired of seeing the American dream be yanked further and further out of reach by politicians who sit in the pocket of lobbyists and corporate PACs.

7. Finally – I ask you to donate because at the end of the day, **I can’t win without you.** This campaign is only possible because of people who step up and support us whenever and however you can.

It's called _Capitol Heat_ , and here's the concept – I sit down with a member of Congress, put a plate of increasingly hot food in front of them, and ask the questions people actually want answered. 😉 My first guest was my friend Derek Tran in CA-45. name: Ruben Gallego
subject: Here's the truth, Peter
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
#

Peter, it’s Ruben.
I know your inbox is full of emails from candidates and campaigns asking for your support.
I know that because my inbox is full of them, too.
For that reason, I try not to reach out to you unless I need to. And when I do, I’m not going to try to scare you into donating. The world is not going to end if you don’t chip in to this email, and one donation of $5 is not going to end Trump’s presidency.
But the truth is, those donations are the largest source of funding we have.
They help support my team — the people I depend on to communicate with millions of people around the country. They help me cover the cost of my travel to and from battleground states. I get asked to come out and help folks quite a bit, and that does cost money. But most of all, it shows the strength of our team.
We built something special in 2024, in my campaign for Senate. And to keep that going, to reach more people, to fight back against Trump, to help win majorities in Congress this November, I do have to ask for donations sometimes.
And when I do, I hope you don’t see it as an annoyance, but as a sign of how important you are to everything I do.
[**Can’t do this without you, Peter. And if you’re willing, I’m humbly asking you to make a donation to my campaign to help power this work. We protected the kids! Or, did we?
# [Why the "Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act" Doesn't Actually Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=10730337&post_id=215385769&utm_source=cross-post&utm_campaign=2114823&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE1Mzg1NzY5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODk1MTEwODAsImV4cCI6MTc5MjEwMzA4MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwNzMwMzM3Iiwic3ViIjoicG9zdC1yZWFjdGlvbiJ9.DLPTJ3NzhT_9KjcN56cj4v-3wqgQeyieofnjf2S-Kww)
### The bill they sold you on protecting all kids doesn't protect all kids
| | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Sep 12

[](https://substack.com/redirect/be9e5e21-48d3-40d6-a3a1-a636cbe24c08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
You might have seen the headline in April. Something about finally making social media companies stop hurting kids.
If you're a mom, you probably felt some kind of relief. Finally. Somebody did something.
But they didn't.
The bill is called the Stop Harms from Addictive Social Media Act (SHASM, if you want the acronym). Idaho signed it April 2. South Carolina passed it in May. Minnesota passed it this spring, almost unanimously.
Its sponsors said the day it was signed that the law tells social media companies they _" can no longer get away with addicting our children."_
In March, a Minnesota committee was told the bill _" protects all teens and kids on social media." _All teens and kids on social media.
That's the sentence I need to talk about, because it isn't true, and the reason is sitting in the bill itself: the new law only applies to companies that make at least $1 billion a year selling ads.
That's the entire test for whether a platform has to follow this new law.
* Do you sell a billion dollars in ads? Then yes.
* Do you make your money some other way? Then no.

The law never asks whether kids get hurt on a platform. It asks how the platform makes money.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/964e37c4-0731-4231-8a1c-013a008a0ca9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Roblox isn't covered by this new law.
Because they don't sell ads for a living. They sell Robux, the little currency your kid begs you for. Kids buy Robux, game developers take a cut, Roblox keeps the rest. Last year that came to $4.9 billion in revenue and nearly $7 billion in bookings.
So how much of that was ad revenue?
In its February letter to shareholders, the company describes its ad revenue as modest, and then says it monetizes a young user base _ "without significant reliance on advertising."_
They wrote that to investors as a selling point. It is also the exact reason this law can't touch them. The law asks how you make your money. Roblox put the answer in writing, and the answer was: not ads.
So Roblox isn't covered. The new law has nothing to say about it. Not one line.
Now look at what else is happening with Roblox right now.
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton sued the company last fall, accusing it of putting **" pixel pedophiles and corporate profit" **ahead of kids' safety. Tennessee's attorney general sued in December and called Roblox the digital equivalent of **a creepy cargo van.** Louisiana, Kentucky, Florida, Oklahoma, and Iowa have all filed lawsuits too. So has Los Angeles County. There's a big federal case in California pulling a lot of these claims together.
These are lawsuits filed by the top law enforcement officer in seven states, saying adults are using this platform to get to children. Yes, the law that was supposed to protect all kids on social media doesn't protect kids on Roblox.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/794fcb59-7509-4ace-8c24-457427ddc558?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Discord gets a pass too.
It's the chat app where a lot of the grooming cases start. And it's named in that same federal case alongside Roblox.
If you made a list of places where American kids get approached by adults who shouldn't be approaching them, Discord is on the first page of it.
But this new law doesn't touch them.
Because Discord makes its money on subscriptions (no real ad business).
Telegram is a messaging app that made $125 million on ads in the first half of last year, out of $870 million total. Untouched.
Then there are the AI companion apps, the chatbots kids talk to for hours at a time. They sell subscriptions, not ads. Texas opened an investigation into Character.AI last year over what those bots were telling children about their own mental health.
The new law doesn't touch them.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9d2f3e3c-bb5a-4dee-81c8-2eec8fc373a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So who does this new bill actually cover?
Facebook and Instagram. TikTok. YouTube. Snapchat. Reddit and Pinterest too.
It's the ad-funded giants. Every one of them is already getting sued by somebody, already dragged in front of Congress, already in every documentary your sister-in-law forwards you. They were getting regulated with or without this law.
And the next one won't be covered either.
Not because it'll be too small. But because of where the money comes from.
The apps kids are moving to sell subscriptions, or currency, or a battle pass, or a premium tier with a better chatbot. Ads are how the last generation of platforms made money. Whatever your kid finds in 18 months will have figured out something else, and this law won't touch them.
It just reaches the apps kids are leaving.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25b15589-2919-47e3-ac2d-74224347f8ce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Sadly, these bills are coming from conservatives.
Not from the left. From us.
And they pass by numbers that should embarrass everyone involved: 62 to 7 in the Idaho House, 132 to 2 in the Minnesota House, 66 to nothing in their Senate.
That happens the same way every time. A bill arrives with a title no one can vote against. Somebody says it will "help the kids." And at that point the hard questions stop getting asked out loud, because asking who this actually covers, in public, on the record, sounds like you're soft on the thing in the title.
So nobody asks (well, almost nobody).
The vote is lopsided, everyone goes home feeling like they did something, and the check on all of it, the part where a conservative reads the text and asks what it really does, gets left at the door.
So it passes, and it reaches you as a news story that says a new law protects kids online, next to a photo of a governor with a pen. The money rule never makes the article. It isn't hidden either. It's the fourth definition in the Idaho bill, on page two.
So what you walk away with is a feeling. Relief.
"The legislature protected my kids!"
Except they didn't. That's just what got sold. Because a mom who knows the law doesn't cover Roblox and Discord keeps checking the iPad. But a mom who was told the law _" protects all teens and kids on social media" _relaxes.
_**The distance between those two moms is exactly where a kid gets hurt, on a platform seven attorneys general are suing right now, that this law doesn 't cover and was never going to cover.**_
It says a billion dollars in ad sales. Roblox told its own investors it doesn't rely on ad sales... but the promise went out to millions of parents anyway.
One more thing worth knowing: the apps it does cover may not survive court. Laws like this have already been struck down in Arkansas, Utah, Ohio, Texas, Louisiana, and Virginia.
Nobody has even sued over this one yet.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8d3d714d-e3c2-4a11-a4e3-968c9ed604f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So, here's what tonight actually looks like:
* Your kid opens Roblox at 9 p.m. - _Not protected_
* Switches to Discord at 10 p.m. - _Not protected_
* Gets a friend request from someone who says he's 14 - _Not protected_
* Finds whatever social media app gets built next spring - _Not protected_

This has been law in Idaho since July 1. It's been in effect for two months. Your kid opened Roblox last night anyway, and he'll open it again tonight, and nothing in Chapter 21 of the Idaho Code has a word to say about it.
There will be lawsuits, deadlines, compliance reports.
_**But none of that is tonight.**_
Because tonight:
* _You decide whether there 's a phone_
* _You decide what 's on it_
* _You decide where it charges overnight (and it isn 't the bedroom)_
* _You pay for the Wi-Fi and the router has a settings page (you 're allowed to use it)_

Your authority covers Roblox. It covers Discord, Snapchat, and the app that hasn't been invented yet. It doesn't have a money rule, it doesn't have an effective date, and no judge anywhere can throw it out.
It's also the only thing on this whole page that works tonight.
No bill makes you a good parent or protects your kids on social media. Not this one, not a better-written one, not the federal version coming behind it.
Only involved parents protect kids.

Senator Ted Cruz has just released a remarkable new book: _**Going Further: The Incomparable Clarence Thomas**_ , built on exclusive interviews with the Justice himself.
