subject: Here’s how we’re building power in MI, PA, and VT:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Meet Katrina, Audrey, Jeff, and Brad.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260915-2&t=1&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)
Exciting news, Peter!
**Leaders We Deserve is proud to announce we’re officially endorsing:**
⭐ **Katrina Manetta** for Michigan HD-58
⭐ **Audrey Grant** for Vermont HD-Caledonia-2
⭐ **Jeff Haylon** for Vermont HD-Rutland-9
⭐ **Brad Chambers** for Pennsylvania HD-41
Before I tell you about each of them — state legislatures play a major role in shaping the reality of people’s everyday lives. They’re where abortion bans get blocked or passed, where Medicaid gets expanded or gutted, where working families either get a seat at the table or get left out entirely while corporations write the rules. That’s why Leaders We Deserve backs bold, people-powered candidates to run in them.
**[Will you split a $5 donation between Katrina, Audrey, Jeff, Brad, and Leaders We Deserve today to help power their campaigns?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&refcode=em20260915-4017&amount=5&t=2&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**[Split a $5 Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=3&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**Katrina Manetta** has always refused to accept broken systems as normal. By refusing to accept something as “just how it is” time and time again, instinct turned into action. She became a community organizer because she was tired of seeing decisions being made that didn’t represent the community. Organizing taught her how to listen, how to mediate between different perspectives, and how to keep people engaged even when change feels slow.
In Macomb County, Katrina will fight to lower costs for Michigan's working families, focusing on housing, groceries, and healthcare. She’ll work to make higher education more affordable for Michiganders and push for higher pay for teachers. And she’ll protect workers and support policies that expand skilled-trades and job training as well as keep high paying jobs in Michigan, working to ensure that new technology doesn’t lead to lower wages or lost jobs.
Her opponent, Republican Ron Robinson has backed expanded concealed carry legislation and stricter voter-ID requirements. This district is a red-blue toss up, but Katrina is exactly the kind of candidate who can flip the seat blue, because she’s been building community and fighting for her neighbors long before this race.
**[Split a Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=4&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**Audrey Grant** grew up in and around Hardwick, VT in rural poverty, and knew her family wasn’t the only one struggling. But watching her mom’s generosity and empathy, despite their own hardships, instilled a love of community, civic engagement, and the natural beauty of the Green Mountain State in Audrey. She has always been a fierce advocate for her neighbors, and holds a strong passion for making government more understandable and accessible. She is the Program Director for the American Legion Auxiliary Green Mountain Girls State and a member of the League of Women Voters Vermont, giving her the opportunity to support Vermont’s youth and civic engagement through various channels.
In Hardwick and Stannard, Audrey will focus on affordability, infrastructure, and local resilience. She will help foster local economic growth and development by supporting community infrastructure projects and in response to yearly flooding in the region, Audrey will push for strengthened disaster relief programs and localized resilience.
This seat is in a community that leans blue, though it’s currently occupied by a Republican. Michael Southworth has voted **against** funding to expand affordable housing, stabilizing community mental health and substance use providers, and other crucial services. Vermonters have previously voted this seat blue, and now Audrey needs your support to flip this seat back and provide the representation her district deserves.
**[Split a Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=5&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**Jeff Haylon** is a businessman and woodworker as well as a two-term Selectboard member. He has also served as a library trustee and on various other boards and communities. Jeff’s unwavering commitment to community and Rutland county has fueled his campaign to flip this seat blue.
In Rutland County, Jeff will focus on lowering costs for Vermonters, addressing high property taxes, housing costs, and giving communities more local control over spending. He also will work towards a single-payer healthcare system and proposes a multi-state healthcare compact. He proposes the consolidation of school districts (_without_ closing local schools) to save on administrative costs while improving student support. Jeff supports funding for public safety alongside investments in social services and working to address the root causes of crime.
District 9 is a district that leans Democratic yet is still held by a Republican. Jeff is running against Aida Nielsen, the wife of the outgoing Republican representative, Todd Nielsen. Aida is an anti-vax nurse and an advisor to her husband during his time in office. Todd has voted against numerous pieces of legislation on conservation and renewable energy, and co-sponsored a bill to decrease vaccination requirements in hospitals. To bring the constituents of Rutland County leadership that truly reflects the community there, Jeff needs your support.
**[Split a Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=6&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**Brad Chambers** has shown he is relentlessly committed to his community and finding solutions that work for the people. He grew up with a single mom and teacher who took on multiple jobs and worked long hours to provide for her children. After graduating college into a depleted job market, he found himself unable to afford housing. This shaped his views on the gap between having a college degree and economic stability. After this period, Brad got involved with PA Furniture Mission, which provides furniture to people getting back on their feet.
In District 41, Brad will push for increasing PA’s share of K-12 education funding while reducing reliance on property taxes. He wants to expand financial support for student teachers and invest in trade and vocational education programs. He supports a single-payer healthcare system that reduces costs and makes coverage more accessible, while lowering prescription drug prices and codifying reproductive rights in the state’s Constitution. Brad will also push to expand access to quality, affordable housing in the county through incentives to build affordable housing, strengthening tenant protections, and fostering programs to support homebuyers.
District 41 is currently represented by Republican Brett Miller, who’s running for re-election. Miller is vehemently anti-choice, voting continuously to take away this right in every possible circumstance. This seat is a toss-up, and Brad needs your support to help flip the seat blue.
**[Split a Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=7&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**Katrina, Audrey, Jeff, and Brad are exactly the kind of young candidates Leaders We Deserve was built to back.** Courageous, deeply rooted in their communities, and not beholden to any corporate donors or special interests. But these leaders need your support to win.
**[If you’re able, can you split a $5 donation between Katrina, Audrey, Jeff, Brad, and Leaders We Deserve today?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&refcode=em20260915-4017&amount=5&t=8&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
**[Split a $5 Donation »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260915_2_state.qiV6wm&amount=5&refcode=em20260915-4017&t=27&akid=4017%2E587540%2EaWTW0C)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

_**Peter**_ , We have a huge election event coming up, and I need your help. Jon Ossoff and I have **two debates** coming up, and I’ll tell you right now, this isn’t just another campaign event. These debates are going to be watched by independents all across Georgia who haven’t made their minds up yet. **And what happens on that stage WILL shape the final days of this entire race.** The polls are tight, we are within the margin of error. Every single undecided voter watching those debates is a vote that goes one way or the other based on what they hear those nights. Peter, It's Becca. **Here's a sentence I never thought I'd have to say out loud: FEMA should not be checking anyone's politics before deciding how much help they get after a disaster.** I know. It sounds absolutely wild. And Vermonters know exactly what I'm talking about. We've lived through some brutal flooding these past few years, and getting help from FEMA already feels like an uphill climb on a good day. Now imagine that on top of the paperwork and the waiting, somebody in Washington is quietly weighing whether your town votes the "right" way before they send help. **This week, I'm taking this fight straight to the House floor to speak in support of a bill that would make that flat-out illegal, permanently, no matter who's in the White House and no matter who's up for reelection.** [_**So if you think disaster relief should depend on need and nothing else, click here and chip in $8, $18, or even $36 today to help me keep fighting for a government that shows up for people no matter how they vote.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139279453/646823754/1803060739?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYTZlZDIzOS01ZGIxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1eAL1-rDEy-sioftTz48rDNms8TWcVVaMx-2P4AChow=) **[FUND HELP, NOT LOYALTY TESTS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/139279454/646823755/1803060739?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYTZlZDIzOS01ZGIxLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1eAL1-rDEy-sioftTz48rDNms8TWcVVaMx-2P4AChow=)** Here's what gets me most about this one. clean_body: Asking because FEMA might. | = Peter, It's Becca. Here's a sentence I never thought I'd have to say out loud: FEMA should not be checking anyone's politics before deciding how much help they get after a disaster. I know. It sounds absolutely wild. And Vermonters know exactly what I'm talking about. We've lived through some brutal flooding these past few years, and getting help from FEMA already feels like an uphill climb on a good day. Now imagine that on top of the paperwork and the waiting, somebody in Washington is quietly weighing whether your town votes the "right" way before they send help. This week, I'm taking this fight straight to the House floor to speak in support of a bill that would make that flat-out illegal, permanently, no matter who's in the White House and no matter who's up for reelection. = = Here's what gets me most about this one. When the water's in your basement or your roof just came off, you're not thinking about elections. You're thinking about your kids, your pets, whether you'll have a bed tonight. Nothing else. The people showing up to help you shouldn't be thinking about anything else either. I ran for Congress because I believe government is supposed to work for people, full stop. Not for whichever party happens to hold the White House that year. Not for anyone's reelection odds. For the family standing in their flooded kitchen wondering who's going to help them clean up. = And look — if this bill passes and the only thing that changes is FEMA staff go back to just doing their actual jobs, I will consider that a genuinely great use of everyone's week. — Becca If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = mailto:beccabalintvt@beccabalint.com | Paid for by Becca Balint for Vermont P.O.
